Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán and _____áji, who had by this time reached the banks of the Mahi river, were now joined by Píláji Gáikwár
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When Kantáji heard that Mubáriz-ul-Mulk had arrived at Pethápur, only eighteen miles from Áhmedábád, he retired to Mehmúdábád. Hámid Khán and Kantáji, who had by this time reached the banks of the Mahi river, were now joined by Píláji Gáikwár.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk deputed his son Khánahzád Khán with an army to oppose them, and made several appointments, among other changes raising Áli _____án to the post of minister
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk deputed his son Khánahzád Khán with an army to oppose them, and made several appointments, among other changes raising Áli Muhammad Khán to the post of minister.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Defeat of the Maráthás at Sojitra and Kapadvanj, _____ Khánahzád Khán met the Maráthás near Sojitra, about ten miles north-west of Petlád, and defeated them, pursuing them as far as the Mahi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Defeat of the Maráthás at Sojitra and Kapadvanj, 1725 Khánahzád Khán met the Maráthás near Sojitra, about ten miles north-west of Petlád, and defeated them, pursuing them as far as the Mahi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Then, returning, he was reinforced by his brother Sháh Nawáz Khán, and marched against the Maráthás, who were encamped at _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Defeat of the Maráthás at Sojitra and Kapadvanj, 1725 Khánahzád Khán met the Maráthás near Sojitra, about ten miles north-west of Petlád, and defeated them, pursuing them as far as the Mahi. Then, returning, he was reinforced by his brother Sháh Nawáz Khán, and marched against the Maráthás, who were encamped at Kapadvanj.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Another battle was fought, and the Maráthás were again defeated and pursued as far as the hills of Áli-Mohan now _____ in the extreme east of the province
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Another battle was fought, and the Maráthás were again defeated and pursued as far as the hills of Áli-Mohan now Chhota Udaipur in the extreme east of the province.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Khánahzád Khán now appointed Hasan-ud-dín governor of Baroda, _____, Jambusar, and Makbulábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Khánahzád Khán now appointed Hasan-ud-dín governor of Baroda, Bharuch, Jambusar, and Makbulábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The Nágars accordingly, seeing no prospect of help, paid a sum of _____ 400000 and Antáji Bháskar retired
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Nágars accordingly, seeing no prospect of help, paid a sum of Rupees 400000 and Antáji Bháskar retired.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kántáji again laid siege to _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Vadnagar was inhabited by wealthy Bráhmans of the Nágar caste who prayed Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to march to their relief; but as both his sons were in pursuit of the other Marátha bands defeated at Kapadvanj, the viceroy had no troops to spare from the Áhmedábád garrison. Kántáji again laid siege to Vadnagar.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shortly afterwards _____ in the Kaira district suffered a similar fate at the hands of Kántáji
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shortly afterwards Umreth in the Kaira district suffered a similar fate at the hands of Kántáji.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In one of his raids Píláji Gáikwár advancing as far as _____ was met by Khánahzád Khán, the son of the viceroy
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In one of his raids Píláji Gáikwár advancing as far as Baroda was met by Khánahzád Khán, the son of the viceroy.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Distrusting the issue of a battle Píláji fled to _____, and from Cambay withdrew to Sorath
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Distrusting the issue of a battle Píláji fled to Cambay, and from Cambay withdrew to Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: For these services the emperor raised Khánahzád Khán to the rank of a noble, with the title Ghálib _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: For these services the emperor raised Khánahzád Khán to the rank of a noble, with the title Ghálib Jang.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Not long afterwards Áli _____án was again entrusted with a command and raised to be governor of Dholka
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Áli Muhammad Khán was dismissed from the post of minister, and in his stead first Muhammad Sayad Beg and afterwards Muhammad Sulaimán were appointed. Not long afterwards Áli Muhammad Khán was again entrusted with a command and raised to be governor of Dholka.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The Maráthás retired to the Dakhan, but, returning in _____, compelled Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to confirm his predecessor's grants in their favour
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Maráthás retired to the Dakhan, but, returning in 1726, compelled Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to confirm his predecessor's grants in their favour.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As part of the agreement between Mubáriz-ul-_____ and the Marátha chiefs Píláji was to receive a share in the revenue of the districts south of the Mahi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Maráthás retired to the Dakhan, but, returning in 1726, compelled Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to confirm his predecessor's grants in their favour. As part of the agreement between Mubáriz-ul-Mulk and the Marátha chiefs Píláji was to receive a share in the revenue of the districts south of the Mahi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time want of funds forced Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to sell the greater part of the _____ district to different landholders
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time want of funds forced Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to sell the greater part of the Dholka district to different landholders.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Though he did not consent to these proposals, the viceroy so far accepted the alliance of the _____ as to allow the governor of Baroda to aid Udáji Pavár against Píláji
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Kántáji, perceiving that if the Peshwa became supreme his own independence would suffer, joined Píláji, and marching together upon Baroda they endeavoured, but without success, to prevent the Mughal governor Sadr-ud-dín Khán from entering the city. In the following year, 1727, Bájiráv Peshwa began to negotiate with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, undertaking that if the one-fourth and one-tenth shares in the revenue of the province were guaranteed to him, he would protect Gujarát from other invaders.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Piláji Gáikwár obtains Baroda and Dabhoi, _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the following year, 1727, Bájiráv Peshwa began to negotiate with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, undertaking that if the one-fourth and one-tenth shares in the revenue of the province were guaranteed to him, he would protect Gujarát from other invaders. Piláji Gáikwár obtains Baroda and Dabhoi, 1727.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Píláji Gáikwár now obtained possession of _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Though he did not consent to these proposals, the viceroy so far accepted the alliance of the Peshwa as to allow the governor of Baroda to aid Udáji Pavár against Píláji. Piláji Gáikwár obtains Baroda and Dabhoi, 1727.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, still sorely pressed for funds, marched into _____ to exact tribute
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, still sorely pressed for funds, marched into Sorath to exact tribute.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On reaching Víramgám, Salábat _____án Bábi, on behalf of the Jám of Nawánagar, presented the viceroy with Rupees 100000, and for this service was rewarded with the gift of an elephant
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: On reaching Víramgám, Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, on behalf of the Jám of Nawánagar, presented the viceroy with Rupees 100000, and for this service was rewarded with the gift of an elephant.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk then marched against Chháya, the capital of the chief of _____ in the south-west of Káthiáwad
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk then marched against Chháya, the capital of the chief of Porbandar in the south-west of Káthiáwad.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: But on hearing that the viceroy proposed to annex his territory and appoint an officer to govern it, he returned and agreed to pay a tribute of _____ 40,000
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: On reaching Víramgám, Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, on behalf of the Jám of Nawánagar, presented the viceroy with Rupees 100000, and for this service was rewarded with the gift of an elephant. But on hearing that the viceroy proposed to annex his territory and appoint an officer to govern it, he returned and agreed to pay a tribute of Rupees 40,000.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time the viceroy received orders from the emperor to restore certain land which he had confiscated, and as he neglected to obey, certain estates of his in the _____áb were resumed
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time the viceroy received orders from the emperor to restore certain land which he had confiscated, and as he neglected to obey, certain estates of his in the Panjáb were resumed.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Capture of Chámpáner by the Maráthás, _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Capture of Chámpáner by the Maráthás, 1728. In 1728 the minister Momín Khán died, and in his place the emperor selected Momín Khán's brother Abd-ul-Ghani Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____ the minister Momín Khán died, and in his place the emperor selected Momín Khán's brother Abd-ul-Ghani Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Capture of Chámpáner by the Maráthás, 1728. In 1728 the minister Momín Khán died, and in his place the emperor selected Momín Khán's brother Abd-ul-Ghani Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time Asad Áli, governor of Junágaḍh, also died, and on his deathbed appointed Salábat _____án Bábi, deputy governor of that fortress
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Asad Áli, governor of Junágaḍh, also died, and on his deathbed appointed Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, deputy governor of that fortress. Salábat Muhammad Khán sent his son Sher Khán Bábi to act on his behalf.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Salábat _____án sent his son Sher Khán Bábi to act on his behalf
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Asad Áli, governor of Junágaḍh, also died, and on his deathbed appointed Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, deputy governor of that fortress. Salábat Muhammad Khán sent his son Sher Khán Bábi to act on his behalf.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When the emperor heard of the death of _____ Áli, he appointed Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, son of the late Asad Áli, governor
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Asad Áli, governor of Junágaḍh, also died, and on his deathbed appointed Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, deputy governor of that fortress. When the emperor heard of the death of Asad Áli, he appointed Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, son of the late Asad Áli, governor.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The Peshwa accordingly sent his brother _____ájiráv to collect the tribute
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Peshwa accordingly sent his brother Chimnájiráv to collect the tribute. Chimnáji plundered Dholka and the country near Chámpáner, while Mubáriz-ul-Mulk exacted tribute from the chiefs on the banks of the Vatrak river.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Chimnáji plundered _____ and the country near Chámpáner, while Mubáriz-ul-Mulk exacted tribute from the chiefs on the banks of the Vatrak river
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Chimnáji plundered Dholka and the country near Chámpáner, while Mubáriz-ul-Mulk exacted tribute from the chiefs on the banks of the Vatrak river.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kántáji now entered _____át and prepared for war in case Chimnáji and the viceroy should unite against him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín did not proceed to Junágaḍh but continued Sher Khán Bábi as his deputy perceiving that neither Píláji nor Kántáji afforded any protection to Gujarát, but rather pillaged it, closed with the offers of Bájiráv Peshwa, and in 1729 formally granted to him the one-fourth and one-tenth shares of the revenue of the province. Kántáji now entered Gujarát and prepared for war in case Chimnáji and the viceroy should unite against him.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: His movements were not interfered with, and after collecting his share of the tribute, he retired to _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: His movements were not interfered with, and after collecting his share of the tribute, he retired to Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The viceroy now marched against the Kolis, and after destroying many of them together with their wives and children, returned to Áhmedábád by way of Modasa and _____ (Himatnagar)
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The viceroy now marched against the Kolis, and after destroying many of them together with their wives and children, returned to Áhmedábád by way of Modasa and Ahmednagar (Himatnagar).

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Through the influence of the viceroy this appointment was not confirmed, and instead Sher Khán Bábi, son of Salábat _____án, was placed in charge of that fortress
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Through the influence of the viceroy this appointment was not confirmed, and instead Sher Khán Bábi, son of Salábat Muhammad Khán, was placed in charge of that fortress.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mulla Muhammad Áli raises a Disturbance at Surat, _____ In Surat, the year 1729, was marked by a severe flood in the Tapti river and by a somewhat serious local disturbance
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mulla Muhammad Áli raises a Disturbance at Surat, 1729 In Surat, the year 1729, was marked by a severe flood in the Tapti river and by a somewhat serious local disturbance.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The chief cause of the disturbance was _____ Áli, a rich Muslim trader of Surat
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mulla Muhammad Áli raises a Disturbance at Surat, 1729 In Surat, the year 1729, was marked by a severe flood in the Tapti river and by a somewhat serious local disturbance. The chief cause of the disturbance was Mulla Muhammad Áli, a rich Muslim trader of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As Píram was not popular, _____ fixed on the village of Athwa, on the left bank of the Tápti, about twelve miles from its mouth
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The chief cause of the disturbance was Mulla Muhammad Áli, a rich Muslim trader of Surat. As Píram was not popular, Mulla Muhammad fixed on the village of Athwa, on the left bank of the Tápti, about twelve miles from its mouth.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Here he began to build a fort, but was ordered to desist by _____áb Khán, the governor of Surat, from which city the proposed stronghold was only three miles distant
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Here he began to build a fort, but was ordered to desist by Sohráb Khán, the governor of Surat, from which city the proposed stronghold was only three miles distant. Accordingly, next day, Beglar-Beg Khán bombarded the governor Sohráb Khán's residence, proclaiming that his own brother Teghbeg Khán was appointed governor of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mulla Muhammad so far from obeying, persuaded Beglar-_____án the commander of the fort of Surat to side with him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mulla Muhammad so far from obeying, persuaded Beglar-Beg Khán the commander of the fort of Surat to side with him. Accordingly, next day, Beglar-Beg Khán bombarded the governor Sohráb Khán's residence, proclaiming that his own brother Teghbeg Khán was appointed governor of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Accordingly, next day, _____-Beg Khán bombarded the governor Sohráb Khán's residence, proclaiming that his own brother Teghbeg Khán was appointed governor of Surat
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mulla Muhammad so far from obeying, persuaded Beglar-Beg Khán the commander of the fort of Surat to side with him. Accordingly, next day, Beglar-Beg Khán bombarded the governor Sohráb Khán's residence, proclaiming that his own brother Teghbeg Khán was appointed governor of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Naḍiád given in Farm, _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Naḍiád given in Farm, 1729. In the same year, 1729, Jawán Mard Khán Bábi was chosen governor of Petlad, Áli Muhammad Khán was made collector of Áhmedábád, and Áli Muhammad's son, the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi and his brother were appointed governor and superintendent of the customs of that district.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Áli _____án shortly resigned and was succeeded by Rú-ín Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the same year, 1729, Jawán Mard Khán Bábi was chosen governor of Petlad, Áli Muhammad Khán was made collector of Áhmedábád, and Áli Muhammad's son, the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi and his brother were appointed governor and superintendent of the customs of that district. Áli Muhammad Khán shortly resigned and was succeeded by Rú-ín Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On the death of Jawán _____án, at the request of Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, his eldest son Kamál-ud-dín Khán Bábi received the districts of Sami and Munjpur and the title of Jawán Mard Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the same year, 1729, Jawán Mard Khán Bábi was chosen governor of Petlad, Áli Muhammad Khán was made collector of Áhmedábád, and Áli Muhammad's son, the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi and his brother were appointed governor and superintendent of the customs of that district. At this time Jawán Mard Khán Bábi, while punishing the Kolis of Bálor, probably Bhátod about fifteen miles east of Bharuch, was killed by a man of that tribe, and in revenge for his death the town of Bálor was plundered.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At the same time the second son, _____, with the title of Safdar Khán, was appointed to the government of Radhanpur
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At the same time the second son, Muhammad Anwar, with the title of Safdar Khán, was appointed to the government of Radhanpur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The viceroy now went to Naḍiád, where Rái Kishandás, agent of Jawán _____án, received the district of Petlád in farm
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At this time Jawán Mard Khán Bábi, while punishing the Kolis of Bálor, probably Bhátod about fifteen miles east of Bharuch, was killed by a man of that tribe, and in revenge for his death the town of Bálor was plundered. On the death of Jawán Mard Khán, at the request of Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, his eldest son Kamál-ud-dín Khán Bábi received the districts of Sami and Munjpur and the title of Jawán Mard Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On his way back to Áhmedábád the viceroy levied tribute from the chief of Umeta, fifteen miles west of _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: From Naḍiád, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk went to collect tribute from Sarḍársingh, the chief of Bhadarva in the Rewa Kántha about fifteen miles north of Baroda, on the banks of the Mahi river, who, after some fighting, agreed to pay a sum of Rs. On his way back to Áhmedábád the viceroy levied tribute from the chief of Umeta, fifteen miles west of Baroda.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As Rái _____ás failed to pay the sum agreed on for the farm of Petlád, an order was issued for his imprisonment
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The viceroy now went to Naḍiád, where Rái Kishandás, agent of Jawán Mard Khán, received the district of Petlád in farm. As Rái Kishandás failed to pay the sum agreed on for the farm of Petlád, an order was issued for his imprisonment.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Athva Fort, _____ When Kántáji returned from Sorath he camped at Sanand, and his advanced guard carried off some of the viceroy's elephants which were grazing there
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Athva Fort, 1730 When Kántáji returned from Sorath he camped at Sanand, and his advanced guard carried off some of the viceroy's elephants which were grazing there.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Meanwhile, at Surat, _____ Áli continued to build the fort at Athva
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Meanwhile, at Surat, Mulla Muhammad Áli continued to build the fort at Athva.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In spite of this the _____ succeeded in persuading Sohráb Khán to allow him to go on with his fort promising in return to get him confirmed as governor of Surat
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Meanwhile, at Surat, Mulla Muhammad Áli continued to build the fort at Athva. At last his accomplice, Beglar-Beg Khán the commander of the Surat fort, began to perceive that if the Athva fort were completed the Mulla would be in a position to obstruct the trade of the port of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As the fort was immediately below _____ the revenue of Surat was greatly diminished, and Sohráb Khán, when it was too late, saw his mistake
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In spite of this the Mulla succeeded in persuading Sohráb Khán to allow him to go on with his fort promising in return to get him confirmed as governor of Surat. As the fort was immediately below Surat the revenue of Surat was greatly diminished, and Sohráb Khán, when it was too late, saw his mistake.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The Viceroy in Káthiáváḍa and Kutch, _____ In 1730, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk went into Gohilwad in south-east Kathiawad and levied tribute from Bhávsingh, chief of Sihor; then he proceeded to Mádhupur, a town
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Viceroy in Káthiáváḍa and Kutch, 1730 In 1730, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk went into Gohilwad in south-east Kathiawad and levied tribute from Bhávsingh, chief of Sihor; then he proceeded to Mádhupur, a town under Porbandar, and laid it waste.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The viceroy now marched in the direction of _____ and refusing the offer of a yearly tribute of about 10,00,000 mahmúdis, advanced against Bhuj
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Viceroy in Káthiáváḍa and Kutch, 1730 In 1730, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk went into Gohilwad in south-east Kathiawad and levied tribute from Bhávsingh, chief of Sihor; then he proceeded to Mádhupur, a town under Porbandar, and laid it waste. The viceroy now marched in the direction of Kutch and refusing the offer of a yearly tribute of about 10,00,000 mahmúdis, advanced against Bhuj.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Riots at Áhmedábád The author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi was ordered to suppress the Áhmedábád riots, which had arisen out of the levy of some fresh taxes, and was invested with the title of _____án
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Riots at Áhmedábád The author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi was ordered to suppress the Áhmedábád riots, which had arisen out of the levy of some fresh taxes, and was invested with the title of Hasan Muhammad Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The friends of order endeavoured to arrange a peaceable transfer between the Mahárája and the late viceroy, but Mubáriz-ul-_____ determined to try the chances of war, and prepared for resistance
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The friends of order endeavoured to arrange a peaceable transfer between the Mahárája and the late viceroy, but Mubáriz-ul-Mulk determined to try the chances of war, and prepared for resistance.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At this time Mír Ismáíl, deputy of Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, arrived and took charge of the government of Junágaḍh from _____án Bábi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At this time Mír Ismáíl, deputy of Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, arrived and took charge of the government of Junágaḍh from Sher Khán Bábi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mahárája _____, after making various appointments, set out with his brother Vakhatsingh and 20,000 men to take over the government of Gujarát
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mahárája Abheysingh, after making various appointments, set out with his brother Vakhatsingh and 20,000 men to take over the government of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When the Mahárája reached _____ he was joined by Safdar Khán Bábi and Jawán Mard Khán Bábi from Radhanpur
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When the Mahárája reached Sidhpur he was joined by Safdar Khán Bábi and Jawán Mard Khán Bábi from Radhanpur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: They then advanced together to Adalaj, distant only about eight miles from _____, their army increasing daily
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: They then advanced together to Adalaj, distant only about eight miles from Ahmedabad, their army increasing daily.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: But as both Mubáriz-ul-_____ and the Mahárája fought disguised as common soldiers, neither party succeeded
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Battle of Adálaj (1730) and Mubáriz-ul-Mulk defeated Mubáriz-ul-Mulk was already encamped between Adálaj and the city, and on the approach of the Mahárája a battle was fought in which the Mahárája was defeated. But as both Mubáriz-ul-Mulk and the Mahárája fought disguised as common soldiers, neither party succeeded.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At first the Mahárája who had the advantage in position repulsed the enemy, but Mubáriz-ul-_____ fought so desperately in the river-bed that the Ráthoḍs gave way
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Battle of Adálaj (1730) and Mubáriz-ul-Mulk defeated Mubáriz-ul-Mulk was already encamped between Adálaj and the city, and on the approach of the Mahárája a battle was fought in which the Mahárája was defeated. But as both Mubáriz-ul-Mulk and the Mahárája fought disguised as common soldiers, neither party succeeded.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: They rallied and made one more desperate charge, but were met, repulsed, and finally pursued as far as _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: They rallied and made one more desperate charge, but were met, repulsed, and finally pursued as far as Sarkhej.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: It was finally agreed that Mubáriz-ul-_____ should receive a sum of 100,000 rupees and should surrender Áhmedábád to the Mahárája
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At first the Mahárája who had the advantage in position repulsed the enemy, but Mubáriz-ul-Mulk fought so desperately in the river-bed that the Ráthoḍs gave way. The Mahárája, who had not expected so determined an opposition, now sent Momín Khán and Amarsingh to negotiate with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, who was still determined to resist to the uttermost.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk accordingly quitted the city and left for Agra by way of _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk accordingly quitted the city and left for Agra by way of Udaipur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shortly afterwards Karímdád Khán Jhálori, governor of Pálanpur, who had accompanied the Mahárája into _____át, died
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shortly afterwards Karímdád Khán Jhálori, governor of Pálanpur, who had accompanied the Mahárája into Gujarát, died.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: After the death of Salábat _____án Bábi, his son, Sher Khán Bábi, was dismissed from the government of Junágaḍh
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: After the death of Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, his son, Sher Khán Bábi, was dismissed from the government of Junágaḍh.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He retired to his estate of _____, and when the Mahárája arrived in Áhmedábád he paid his respects, presenting the viceroy with an elephant and some horses
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He retired to his estate of Ghogha, and when the Mahárája arrived in Áhmedábád he paid his respects, presenting the viceroy with an elephant and some horses.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Momín Khán Ruler of Cambay, _____ Momín Khán was made ruler of Cambay, and Fidá-ud-dín Khán, his cousin, was made governor of the lands near that city, the revenue of which had been assigned to the Ma
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Momín Khán Ruler of Cambay, 1730 Momín Khán was made ruler of Cambay, and Fidá-ud-dín Khán, his cousin, was made governor of the lands near that city, the revenue of which had been assigned to the Mahárája.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: So great was the fear of the Maráthás, that _____íd Khán, the governor elect of Surat, instead of proceeding direct by land, went to Cambay
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: So great was the fear of the Maráthás, that Mustafíd Khán, the governor elect of Surat, instead of proceeding direct by land, went to Cambay. Píláji agreed, but Sohráb Khán, who was still in possession of Surat, refused to hand it over to Mustafíd Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Píláji agreed, but Sohráb Khán, who was still in possession of Surat, refused to hand it over to _____íd Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: So great was the fear of the Maráthás, that Mustafíd Khán, the governor elect of Surat, instead of proceeding direct by land, went to Cambay. Píláji agreed, but Sohráb Khán, who was still in possession of Surat, refused to hand it over to Mustafíd Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: From Cambay he moved to _____, and from Bharuch entered into negotiations with Píláji Gáikwár, promising, if allowed to retain possession of Surat, to pay Píláji the one-fourth share of its revenues
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: From Cambay he moved to Bharuch, and from Bharuch entered into negotiations with Píláji Gáikwár, promising, if allowed to retain possession of Surat, to pay Píláji the one-fourth share of its revenues.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In this year also _____, brother of the Mahárája Abheysingh, was appointed governor of Pátan, and sent a deputy to act for him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In this year also Vakhatsingh, brother of the Mahárája Abheysingh, was appointed governor of Pátan, and sent a deputy to act for him.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When he proceeded to take up his appointment he was opposed by Mír Ismáíl, and was killed in a battle fought near _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When he proceeded to take up his appointment he was opposed by Mír Ismáíl, and was killed in a battle fought near Amreli.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The Peshwa and Viceroy against Piláji Gáikwár, _____ In 1731, Bájiráv Peshwa, entering Gujarát at the head of an army, advanced against Baroda, then in the possession of Píláji Gáikwár
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Peshwa and Viceroy against Piláji Gáikwár, 1731 In 1731, Bájiráv Peshwa, entering Gujarát at the head of an army, advanced against Baroda, then in the possession of Píláji Gáikwár.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At this meeting it was agreed that Bájiráv should assist Ázmatulláh, the governor of _____, in taking possession of that town and in expelling Píláji Gáikwár
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Peshwa and Viceroy against Piláji Gáikwár, 1731 In 1731, Bájiráv Peshwa, entering Gujarát at the head of an army, advanced against Baroda, then in the possession of Píláji Gáikwár. At this meeting it was agreed that Bájiráv should assist Ázmatulláh, the governor of Baroda, in taking possession of that town and in expelling Píláji Gáikwár.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Accordingly, the _____, together with an army from the viceroy, marched on Baroda
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: By this arrangement the viceroy hoped by playing off the Peshwa against Píláji, to succeed in getting rid of the latter, while the Peshwa intended that if Píláji was forced to give up Baroda, he himself should gain possession of that city. Accordingly, the Peshwa, together with an army from the viceroy, marched on Baroda.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: They had scarcely laid siege to the city when the _____ heard that Nizám-ul-Mulk was advancing on Gujarát against him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: By this arrangement the viceroy hoped by playing off the Peshwa against Píláji, to succeed in getting rid of the latter, while the Peshwa intended that if Píláji was forced to give up Baroda, he himself should gain possession of that city. Accordingly, the Peshwa, together with an army from the viceroy, marched on Baroda.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Abandoning all operations against _____, the Peshwa withdrew, with all speed, to the Dakhan
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: By this arrangement the viceroy hoped by playing off the Peshwa against Píláji, to succeed in getting rid of the latter, while the Peshwa intended that if Píláji was forced to give up Baroda, he himself should gain possession of that city. Accordingly, the Peshwa, together with an army from the viceroy, marched on Baroda.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: An engagement was fought in which the Peshwa was victorious and _____áv was slain
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: On his way he encountered the army of Trimbakráv Senápati, who, together with Piláji Kántáji and Udáji Pavár, had united to resist the pretensions of the Peshwa in Gujarát, and were also secretly leagued with the Nizám. An engagement was fought in which the Peshwa was victorious and Trimbakráv was slain.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Abdúlláh Beg appointed the Nizám's _____ at Broach
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Abdúlláh Beg appointed the Nizám's Deputy at Broach. Dissatisfied that the government of Gujarát should be in the hands of Abheysingh, Abdúlláh Beg, in 1731, entered into negotiations with the Nizám, offering to hold Bharuch as the Nizám's deputy.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Dissatisfied that the government of Gujarát should be in the hands of Abheysingh, Abdúlláh Beg, in _____, entered into negotiations with the Nizám, offering to hold Bharuch as the Nizám's deputy
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Dissatisfied that the government of Gujarát should be in the hands of Abheysingh, Abdúlláh Beg, in 1731, entered into negotiations with the Nizám, offering to hold Bharuch as the Nizám's deputy.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Nizám-ul-_____ agreed, appointed Abdúlláh his deputy, and ennobled him with the title of Nek Álam Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: During these changes the city of Bharuch, which on account of the strength of its fort the Maráthás had failed to take, was governed by Abdúlláh Beg, an officer originally appointed to that command by Mubáriz-ul-Mulk. Nizám-ul-Mulk agreed, appointed Abdúlláh his deputy, and ennobled him with the title of Nek Álam Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About the same time _____, brother of the viceroy, withdrew to his chiefship of Nágor in Jodhpur, and Ázmat-ulláh went to Ágra
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About the same time Vakhatsingh, brother of the viceroy, withdrew to his chiefship of Nágor in Jodhpur, and Ázmat-ulláh went to Ágra.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Momín Khán received the farm of _____, and Kántáji was confirmed in the share he had acquired of the revenues of Gujarát
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Momín Khán received the farm of Petlad, and Kántáji was confirmed in the share he had acquired of the revenues of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____ the paymaster, Amánatdár Khán, died, and was succeeded by Ghulám Hasan Khán, who sent Mujáhid-ud-dín Khán to act as his deputy
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1732 the paymaster, Amánatdár Khán, died, and was succeeded by Ghulám Hasan Khán, who sent Mujáhid-ud-dín Khán to act as his deputy.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Through the influence of _____, Sohráb Áli was now confirmed as governor of Surat, and Mustafíd Khán was obliged to return to Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Through the influence of Mulla Muhammad Ali, Sohráb Áli was now confirmed as governor of Surat, and Mustafíd Khán was obliged to return to Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The recent acquisition of the town of _____ and of the strong fortress of Dabhoi had made Piláji still more formidable
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The recent acquisition of the town of Baroda and of the strong fortress of Dabhoi had made Piláji still more formidable. Under these circumstances, Abheysingh, who had long wished to recover Baroda and Dabhoi determined to assassinate Piláji, and this was effected by a Márvádi at the village of Dakor.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: They then evacuated the district of _____, retiring to the fortress of Dabhoi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The recent acquisition of the town of Baroda and of the strong fortress of Dabhoi had made Piláji still more formidable. Under these circumstances, Abheysingh, who had long wished to recover Baroda and Dabhoi determined to assassinate Piláji, and this was effected by a Márvádi at the village of Dakor.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Under these circumstances, _____, who had long wished to recover Baroda and Dabhoi determined to assassinate Piláji, and this was effected by a Márvádi at the village of Dakor
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Píláji Gáikwár as the agent of the deceased Khanderáv Dábháde Senápati, as the owner of the fort of Songad, and as the ally of the Bhíls and Kolis, was naturally a thorn in the side of the viceroy Abheysingh. Under these circumstances, Abheysingh, who had long wished to recover Baroda and Dabhoi determined to assassinate Piláji, and this was effected by a Márvádi at the village of Dakor.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On hearing of the death of Píláji, the viceroy immediately advanced against the Maráthás, and, after taking possession of _____, laid siege to Dabhoi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Under these circumstances, Abheysingh, who had long wished to recover Baroda and Dabhoi determined to assassinate Piláji, and this was effected by a Márvádi at the village of Dakor. The Maráthás slew the assassin and withdrew across the Mahi, burning the body of Piláji at the village of Savli, fourteen miles north of Baroda.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He then went to _____, and after placing Sher Khán Bábi in charge of the city, returned to Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: They then evacuated the district of Baroda, retiring to the fortress of Dabhoi. On hearing of the death of Píláji, the viceroy immediately advanced against the Maráthás, and, after taking possession of Baroda, laid siege to Dabhoi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____, Gujarát was wasted by famine
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1732, Gujarát was wasted by famine. Affairs at Surat, 1732.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Meanwhile, at Surat Múlla _____ of Athva was again the cause of disturbance
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Meanwhile, at Surat Múlla Muhammad Ali of Athva was again the cause of disturbance.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The messengers bearing these communications were intercepted at Broach by the partisans of _____, who determined to remove this powerful cause of anxiety
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Resisting with force the demand of a sum of 100,000 rupees by Sohráb Khán, the governor of Surat, he succeeded in driving Sohráb Khán out of the city, and the government of Surat was then usurped by Teghbeg Khán, a brother of Beglar-Beg Khán. The messengers bearing these communications were intercepted at Broach by the partisans of Teghbeg, who determined to remove this powerful cause of anxiety.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Teghbeg Khán, inviting Muhammad Ali to an entertainment, placed him in confinement, and after keeping him in prison for two years, in _____ put him to death
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Teghbeg Khán, inviting Muhammad Ali to an entertainment, placed him in confinement, and after keeping him in prison for two years, in 1734 put him to death.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Teghbeg also took possession of the fort of _____, and plundered it
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Teghbeg also took possession of the fort of Athva, and plundered it.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Sohráb Khán, seeing that he could not recover Surat, went with _____ to Ghogha, where his relatives lived, and from that, proceeding to Bhavnagar settled there
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Sohráb Khán, seeing that he could not recover Surat, went with Sayad Wali to Ghogha, where his relatives lived, and from that, proceeding to Bhavnagar settled there.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When the emperor heard what had happened, he appointed Momín Khán to Surat and _____án to Cambay
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Teghbeg Khán, inviting Muhammad Ali to an entertainment, placed him in confinement, and after keeping him in prison for two years, in 1734 put him to death. When the emperor heard what had happened, he appointed Momín Khán to Surat and Teghbeg Khán to Cambay.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Momín Khán sent Sayad Núrullah to act for him, but he was defeated by Teghbeg Khán, who afterwards contrived, in _____, to be formally appointed governor of Surat with the title of Bahádur
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Momín Khán sent Sayad Núrullah to act for him, but he was defeated by Teghbeg Khán, who afterwards contrived, in 1733, to be formally appointed governor of Surat with the title of Bahádur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Collecting an army and taking with her Kántáji _____ and Dámáji Gáikwár, son of Píláji, she marched upon Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Collecting an army and taking with her Kántáji Kadam and Dámáji Gáikwár, son of Píláji, she marched upon Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: For his services on this occasion Jawán _____án was made governor of Viramgam
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the end it was agreed that in addition to the one-fourth and the one-tenth shares of the revenue a sum of rupees 80,000 should be paid from the Áhmedábád treasury, Jawán Mard Khán being kept as a hostage till the payments were made. For his services on this occasion Jawán Mard Khán was made governor of Viramgam.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: During this year an imperial order appointed Khushálchand Sheth, son of _____, Nagar Sheth or chief merchant of Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: During this year an imperial order appointed Khushálchand Sheth, son of Shantidas Jhaveri, Nagar Sheth or chief merchant of Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Umábái now marched upon _____, and the governor, Sher Khán Bábi, prepared to oppose the Maráthás
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Umábái now marched upon Baroda, and the governor, Sher Khán Bábi, prepared to oppose the Maráthás.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____, Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, governor of Junágaḍh died, and his son Mír Hazabr Khán was selected to fill his place
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1733, Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, governor of Junágaḍh died, and his son Mír Hazabr Khán was selected to fill his place.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Meanwhile, as the Maráthás had not received their rights, Jádoji Dábháde, son of Umábái, returned to _____át
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Meanwhile, as the Maráthás had not received their rights, Jádoji Dábháde, son of Umábái, returned to Gujarát.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Peace was concluded on the former basis, and Jádoji marched into _____ to exact tribute
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Peace was concluded on the former basis, and Jádoji marched into Sorath to exact tribute. In the meantime Sohráb Khán, the former governor of Surat, who had been kindly received by Bhávsinghji, the chief of Sihor, began to raise a following and was appointed collector of arrears in Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In the meantime Sohráb Khán, the former governor of Surat, who had been kindly received by Bhávsinghji, the chief of Sihor, began to raise a following and was appointed collector of arrears in _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Peace was concluded on the former basis, and Jádoji marched into Sorath to exact tribute. In the meantime Sohráb Khán, the former governor of Surat, who had been kindly received by Bhávsinghji, the chief of Sihor, began to raise a following and was appointed collector of arrears in Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In this year the _____ of the Chúnvál and Kánkrej committed many excesses, and a Rájput noble was robbed in the Pátan district
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In this year the Kolis of the Chúnvál and Kánkrej committed many excesses, and a Rájput noble was robbed in the Pátan district.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He chose _____ Núrullah as his deputy, and sent him to recover the revenue for the current year
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He chose Sayad Núrullah as his deputy, and sent him to recover the revenue for the current year.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At this time _____án Bábi was at Baroda, and his younger brother, though he resisted, was compelled to leave Ghogha
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: On the death of Salábat Khán Bábi, though the Mahárája had endeavoured to get Sher Khán Bábi appointed in place of his father, Ghogha had been granted to Burhán-ul-Mulk, who chose Sohráb Khán as his deputy. At this time Sher Khán Bábi was at Baroda, and his younger brother, though he resisted, was compelled to leave Ghogha.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The deputy governor of _____ complained to the governor of the oppressive conduct of Sohráb Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The deputy governor of Sorath complained to the governor of the oppressive conduct of Sohráb Khán. But Burhán-ul-Mulk supported Sohráb and having obtained for himself the government of Sorath, sent Sohráb Khán as his deputy to Junágaḍh.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____, Ratansingh Bhandári, the deputy viceroy, ordered Bhávsingh, son of Udaikaran, the hereditary officer of Víramgám, to be captured by Jawán-Mard Khán, imprisoned and sent him to Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1734, Ratansingh Bhandári, the deputy viceroy, ordered Bhávsingh, son of Udaikaran, the hereditary officer of Víramgám, to be captured by Jawán-Mard Khán, imprisoned and sent him to Áhmedábád. Baroda recovered by the Maráthás, 1734 In 1734, Sher Khán Bábi, governor of Baroda, went to visit his lands at Balasinor, leaving Muhammad Sarbáz in command at Baroda, Máhadáji Gáikwár, brother of Píláji, who then held Jambúsar, sending to Songad to Dámáji for aid, marched on Baroda with a strong force.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Jawan-_____án went so far as to arrest Bhávsingh, but was forced by his supporters to release him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1734, Ratansingh Bhandári, the deputy viceroy, ordered Bhávsingh, son of Udaikaran, the hereditary officer of Víramgám, to be captured by Jawán-Mard Khán, imprisoned and sent him to Áhmedábád. Jawan-Mard Khán went so far as to arrest Bhávsingh, but was forced by his supporters to release him.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Momín Khán, who arrived after _____án's defeat, did not deem it prudent to engage the Maráthás, and retired to Cambay
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The garrison made a brave defence, and Sher Khán hearing of the attack at Bálásinor, called for aid from Ratansingh Bhandári, the deputy viceroy, who directed Momín Khán, the governor of Cambay, to join Sher Khán and drive back the Maráthás. Sher Khán started at once for Baroda.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In the meantime the garrison of Baroda, hopeless of succour, surrendered the town, and since that day Baroda continued to be the headquarters of the Gáikwár family until independence of India in _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the meantime the garrison of Baroda, hopeless of succour, surrendered the town, and since that day Baroda continued to be the headquarters of the Gáikwár family until independence of India in 1947.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At this time Dhanrúp Bhandári, governor of Petlád, died, and the farm of the districts of Nadiad, Arhar-Mátar, Petlád, and _____ was given to Momín Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At this time Dhanrúp Bhandári, governor of Petlád, died, and the farm of the districts of Nadiad, Arhar-Mátar, Petlád, and Mahudha was given to Momín Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mulla Muhammad Áli managed to write letters from his confinement at Surat to the Nizám; and as that chief was now not far from Surat, he wrote urgently to _____án to release him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mulla Muhammad Áli managed to write letters from his confinement at Surat to the Nizám; and as that chief was now not far from Surat, he wrote urgently to Teghbeg Khán to release him. Teghbeg Khán put the Mulla to death, and bribing the Nizám's messenger, gave out that he had died of joy at his release.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Khushálchand, the chief of the merchants of Áhmedábád, having had a difference with _____, was forced to leave the city, and sought shelter at Cambay and afterwards at Junágaḍh
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Khushálchand, the chief of the merchants of Áhmedábád, having had a difference with Ratansingh, was forced to leave the city, and sought shelter at Cambay and afterwards at Junágaḍh.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Jawán _____án conceived the design of conquering Idar from Anandsingh and Ráisingh, brothers of the Mahárája Abheysingh
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Jawán Mard Khán conceived the design of conquering Idar from Anandsingh and Ráisingh, brothers of the Mahárája Abheysingh. The Marátha chiefs at once marched to the help of Ídar, and Jawán Mard Khán, disbelieving the report of Marátha aid, continued to advance until he found himself opposed by an overwhelming force.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He accordingly marched upon Ídar, taking with him as allies Aghráji Koli of Katosan and _____ of Ilol Kánrah
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He accordingly marched upon Ídar, taking with him as allies Aghráji Koli of Katosan and Koli Amra of Ilol Kánrah.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In this strait _____ and Ráisingh sought the aid of Malhárráv Holkar and Ránoji Sindia, who were at this time in Málwa
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Jawán Mard Khán conceived the design of conquering Idar from Anandsingh and Ráisingh, brothers of the Mahárája Abheysingh. In this strait Anandsingh and Ráisingh sought the aid of Malhárráv Holkar and Ránoji Sindia, who were at this time in Málwa.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Negotiations were entered into, and Jawán _____án agreed to pay a sum of Rupees 1,75,000

Negotiations were entered into, and Jawán Mard Khán agreed to pay a sum of Rupees 1,75,000.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Negotiations were entered into, and Jawán Mard Khán agreed to pay a sum of Rupees 1,75,000. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In this year Teghbeg Khán of Surat caused a wealthy merchant named Áhmed Chalabi to be assassinated, and confiscated his property.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: From Koth he advanced and pitched at Harala, about ten miles from Sohráb Khán's camp, and here he was joined by Momín Khán and others whom he had summoned to support him.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Defeat and Death of Sohráb Khán, 1735 After the union of these forces he marched to Dholi, six miles from Dhandhuka, at which place Sohráb Khán was then encamped.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He was buried at Sihor in Kathiwar.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Rivalry between Ratansingh Bhandári and Momín Khán, _____ After this success a single horseman attacked and wounded Ratansingh Bhandári in two places
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rivalry between Ratansingh Bhandári and Momín Khán, 1735 After this success a single horseman attacked and wounded Ratansingh Bhandári in two places.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rivalry between Ratansingh Bhandári and Momín Khán, 1735 After this success a single horseman attacked and wounded Ratansingh Bhandári in two places. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kaliánchand, was appointed to Víramgám in place of _____án Bábi, and instead of Sohráb Khán, Muhsin Khán Khálvi was made deputy governor of Sorath
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Kaliánchand, was appointed to Víramgám in place of Sher Khán Bábi, and instead of Sohráb Khán, Muhsin Khán Khálvi was made deputy governor of Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Battle of Ánand-Mogri, _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Battle of Ánand-Mogri, 1735.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time Dámáji Gáikwár, who had been chosen by Umábái as her representative in Gujarát, appointed _____ to act as his agent
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Dámáji Gáikwár, who had been chosen by Umábái as her representative in Gujarát, appointed Rangoji to act as his agent. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kántáji being dissatisfied with this arrangement, in which his rights were ignored, marched into _____át
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Dámáji Gáikwár, who had been chosen by Umábái as her representative in Gujarát, appointed Rangoji to act as his agent. Kántáji being dissatisfied with this arrangement, in which his rights were ignored, marched into Gujarát.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Rangoji met him, and a battle was fought at Ánand-_____, twenty-five miles south-east of Kheda, in which Kántáji was defeated and his son killed
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Battle of Ánand-Mogri, 1735. Rangoji met him, and a battle was fought at Ánand-Mogri, twenty-five miles south-east of Kheda, in which Kántáji was defeated and his son killed.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In consequence of this reverse Kántáji retired to _____ád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In consequence of this reverse Kántáji retired to Petlád. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As the districts where these battles were fought were held in farm by _____án Bábi, he suffered much loss, and consequently retired to Rádhanpur
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: As the districts where these battles were fought were held in farm by Safdar Khán Bábi, he suffered much loss, and consequently retired to Rádhanpur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Rangoji was joined by Dámáji Gáikwár, and these two leaders went together to _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rangoji was joined by Dámáji Gáikwár, and these two leaders went together to Dholka.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Leaving Rangoji at Víramgám, Dámáji marched into _____ to levy tribute from the chiefs, and after collecting a portion of his dues, returned to the Dakhan
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Leaving Rangoji at Víramgám, Dámáji marched into Sorath to levy tribute from the chiefs, and after collecting a portion of his dues, returned to the Dakhan.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Meanwhile, though _____ had summoned Momín Khán to his aid, he delayed coming, as he began to scheme independence at Cambay
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Ratansingh Bhandári, the deputy viceroy, marched against him, and forced him to retire to Víramgám. Ratansingh pursued the Maráthás to Víramgám, attacked and defeated them capturing their baggage, but failed to prevent them taking shelter in the town.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Here, through _____áíl, the governor of Dholka, he demanded from the Bhandári his share of the revenue
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Here, through Muhammad Ismáíl, the governor of Dholka, he demanded from the Bhandári his share of the revenue.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Afterwards, leaving _____ horse in Dholka, he went to Dhandhúka
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Afterwards, leaving 2000 horse in Dholka, he went to Dhandhúka.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In the meantime Kántáji, who was a follower of Bájiráv _____, joining with Malhárráv Holkar, advanced upon Ídar, and coming against Dánta, plundered that town
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the meantime Kántáji, who was a follower of Bájiráv Peshwa, joining with Malhárráv Holkar, advanced upon Ídar, and coming against Dánta, plundered that town.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Some Nágar Bráhmans of the town of _____, who were settled in Dánta, tried to escape to the hills, but were intercepted and pillaged
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Some Nágar Bráhmans of the town of Vadnagar, who were settled in Dánta, tried to escape to the hills, but were intercepted and pillaged. The Maráthás then proceeded to Vadnagar and plundered the town.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kántáji and Malhárráv _____ then marched into Márwár, while Pratápráv and Rangoji crossed over from Dhandhuka into Káthiáváḍa and Gohilváḍa
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the meantime Kántáji, who was a follower of Bájiráv Peshwa, joining with Malhárráv Holkar, advanced upon Ídar, and coming against Dánta, plundered that town. Kántáji and Malhárráv Holkar then marched into Márwár, while Pratápráv and Rangoji crossed over from Dhandhuka into Káthiáváḍa and Gohilváḍa.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time _____ár Khán Jhálori was appointed deputy governor of Pátan on behalf of Vakhatsingh
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Muhammad Pahár Khán Jhálori was appointed deputy governor of Pátan on behalf of Vakhatsingh.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As no settlement of his demands on the revenues of Dholka had yet been made, Pratápráv returned to that town and sent _____ to receive the tribute due to him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: As no settlement of his demands on the revenues of Dholka had yet been made, Pratápráv returned to that town and sent Narhar Pandit to receive the tribute due to him.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Afterwards proceeding to _____ with Rangoji they were summoned to Sorath by Dámáji to assist him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Afterwards proceeding to Baroda with Rangoji they were summoned to Sorath by Dámáji to assist him.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Afterwards on Momín Khán's remonstrance Subháchand Márvádi was appointed to examine the accounts and receive the revenue in place of _____án
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Sher Khán Bábi, who up to his time had been at Kaira, now came to Áhmedábád, and as the deputy viceroy was displeased with Momín Khán's conduct when Víramgám was besieged, he appointed Sher Khán his own deputy at Petlád, Arhar-Mátar, and Naḍiád. Afterwards on Momín Khán's remonstrance Subháchand Márvádi was appointed to examine the accounts and receive the revenue in place of Sher Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Momín Khán seeing that _____án had not yet left Kaira, collected some men and came to Petlád, while Sher Khán went to Dehgam and awaited the departure of Rangoji
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Sher Khán Bábi, who up to his time had been at Kaira, now came to Áhmedábád, and as the deputy viceroy was displeased with Momín Khán's conduct when Víramgám was besieged, he appointed Sher Khán his own deputy at Petlád, Arhar-Mátar, and Naḍiád. Afterwards on Momín Khán's remonstrance Subháchand Márvádi was appointed to examine the accounts and receive the revenue in place of Sher Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____ Dámáji's brother Pratápráv, returning to his country after exacting tribute from the chiefs of Sorath, died of smallpox at Kánkar near Dholka
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1737 Dámáji's brother Pratápráv, returning to his country after exacting tribute from the chiefs of Sorath, died of smallpox at Kánkar near Dholka.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: As he was unable to effect anything by himself he persuaded Jawán Mard Khán Bábi to join him by a promise of the government of Pátan and directed him to proceed and take up that appointment. Now the Jháloris were allies of the Ráthoḍs, and Pahár Khán Jhálori, then in command of Pátan, opposed Jawán Mard Khán, but was finally obliged to vacate Pátan.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: As he was unable to effect anything by himself he persuaded Jawán Mard Khán Bábi to join him by a promise of the government of Pátan and directed him to proceed and take up that appointment. Now the Jháloris were allies of the Ráthoḍs, and Pahár Khán Jhálori, then in command of Pátan, opposed Jawán Mard Khán, but was finally obliged to vacate Pátan.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: This alliance with the Maráthás gave the last blow to _____ power in Gujarát, which otherwise might have lingered for at least a quarter of a century
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: This alliance with the Maráthás gave the last blow to Mughal power in Gujarát, which otherwise might have lingered for at least a quarter of a century.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Meanwhile, he sent officials to _____ to persuade Momín Khán to take no further steps until a reply should be received to the reference Momín Khán had made to Ágra
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rangoji agreed to aid him in expelling the Márvádis, on condition that, if successful, he should be granted one-half of the produce of Gujarát except the city of Áhmedábád, the lands in the neighbourhood of the city, and the port of Cambay. Meanwhile, he sent officials to Cambay to persuade Momín Khán to take no further steps until a reply should be received to the reference Momín Khán had made to Ágra.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The reply of the Mahárája was that _____ should resist Momín Khán if he could
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When Ratansingh Bhandári heard of the appointment of Momín Khán to be viceroy, he wrote to Mahárája Abheysingh for orders. The reply of the Mahárája was that Ratansingh should resist Momín Khán if he could.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About the same time Momín Khán's manager, Vajerám, whom he had sent to Songad to solicit Dámáji to march in person to his assistance, arrived and informed him that Dámáji would join him shortly.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Some of the Mahárája's guns, which were being sent to Áhmedábád by his agents at Surat through _____ for facility of transit, were about this time captured by a party of Momín Khán's men
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Some of the Mahárája's guns, which were being sent to Áhmedábád by his agents at Surat through Cambay for facility of transit, were about this time captured by a party of Momín Khán's men.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The nobles fearing the consequences, recalled him, and persuaded the emperor to re-appoint him viceroy of _____át
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The nobles fearing the consequences, recalled him, and persuaded the emperor to re-appoint him viceroy of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shortly before this Muhammad Bákir Khán, son of Muâtamid Khán, joined Momín Khán from Surat, while Sádik Áli Khán and his nephew reinforced him from Junágaḍh.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Dámáji Gáikwár now joined Momín Khán from _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Dámáji Gáikwár now joined Momín Khán from Songad.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When Ratansingh Bhandári heard of the arrangements made between Dámáji and Momín Khán, he sent a message to Dámáji saying, 'Momín Khán has promised Rangoji half of the revenues of Gujarát excepting the city of Áhmedábád, the lands immediately round it, and Cambay. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When Ratansingh Bhandári heard of the arrangements made between Dámáji and Momín Khán, he sent a message to Dámáji saying, 'Momín Khán has promised Rangoji half of the revenues of Gujarát excepting the city of Áhmedábád, the lands immediately round it, and Cambay. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Momín Khán now sent the writer of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi to Ratansingh Bhandári, in hopes that he might withdraw peaceably, but Ratansingh refused to listen to any terms.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Dámáji, who in the meantime had been to Sorath, now returned and was met by _____, who accompanied him as far as the banks of the Mahi, whence Rangoji proceeded to Dholka
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Dámáji, who in the meantime had been to Sorath, now returned and was met by Rangoji, who accompanied him as far as the banks of the Mahi, whence Rangoji proceeded to Dholka. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The city was thus equally divided, and the Astodia and Raipur gates were guarded by the Maráthás.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: After spending a few days at Dholka, Rangoji returned to Áhmedábád and took charge of his share of the city, which comprised the Raikhad, Khánjchán, and Jamalpur quarters as far as the Astoria and Ráipur gates. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Momín Khán, though secretly pleased, affected ignorance and sent Fidá-ud-dín Khán to reassure Rangoji. This with some difficulty he succeeded in doing and Rangoji remained in the city.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Jawán Mard Khán was sent to Pátan, and, instead of Prántij, the district of Kheralu was granted to Zoráwar Khán Bábi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: From Mánsa they proceeded to Kadi, and from Kadi to Víjápur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Viceroy collects Tribute, 1738 When Momín Khán arrived at Ídar, Ánandsingh and Ráisingh, brothers of Mahárája Abheysingh, went to him and paid the tribute of Mohanpur and Ranásan as being within the limits of the Ídar territory.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Guru Nanak.subject: Ancient India
Guru Nanak.question: The cobra version is sourced from the _____ janamsakhi tradition
Guru Nanak.fact: Nanak's father hoped his son would take up accounting or mercantile work but Nanak was more interested in religious pursuits, spending much of his time outside, often discussing subjects with sadhus and sufis or roaming the local wilderness.  Nanak also spent much time taking care of the family's cattle in the fields, as his father noticed he seemed happier outdoors than indoors.  Other stories of his childhood refer to strange and miraculous events about Nanak, such as the one witnessed by Rai Bular, in which the sleeping child's head was shaded from the harsh sunlight by, in one account, by the stationary shadow of a tree, or in another, by a venomous cobra.  The cobra version is sourced from the Bala janamsakhi tradition.  An early miraculous story found in Sikh literature is one where Nanak was watching over his family's buffalos when they rampaged into a neighbouring field, destroying crops.  However, when the condition of the crops were checked, they were mysteriously unharmed (the location of the field is now marked by Gurdwara Kiara Sahib in Nankana Sahib). At the age of nine, Nanak began composing his own poetry, being influenced by bhagats and Sufis

The second theory states that Nanak was a Guru, not a prophet.  According to Singha (2009): Sikhism does not subscribe to the theory of incarnation or the concept of prophet hood.  But it has a pivotal concept of Guru.  He is not an incarnation of God, not even a prophet

Guru Nanak favoured the salok in his writings, consisting of an internal divide of two half-verses which end with a rhyme.  The guru wrote long sequences of rhyming stanzas consisting of basic units, to provide a spiritual message that is clearly articulated.  The languages utilized in his compositions consists of archaic Punjabi and Khariboli, with many Persian loanwords.  Rather than only writing in the elite languages, such as Arabic, Persian, or Sanskrit, Nanak makes use of the vernacular Punjabi in his works to reach a wider audience.  However, Nanak chose to include more Saraiki vocabulary in some works whilst consciously chose to use more Hindi or Sanskritic words when delving into Hindu religious topics. Guru Nanak.fact: Nanak wrote using similies, analogies, and metaphors to explain phislophical concepts.  He positions himself as being a slave of the divine in his works.  Much of his works, such as in the Japji, are inquisitive in-nature, pondering upon the nature and purpose of the Universe or life itself yet not accepting any prevailing theories or claiming to know the answer, leaving the audience in a state of deep reflection and wonder.  He spreads the message of love rather than hatred in his hymns and that it was more important to be a good human-being than being a "good Muslim" or "good Hindu".  Guru Arjan collected and included 974 hymns authored by Nanak in his Ād Granth compilation in 1604, with the Japji forming the opening of the work, with all subsequent works by the Sikh gurus being modelled after Guru Nanak's.  == Influences == Many Sikhs believe that Nanak's message was divinely revealed, as his own words in Guru Granth Sahib state that his teachings are as he has received them from the Creator Himself. Lewis, due to how ambiguous it is and how the term has been selectively used to describe Sikhism in academia despite evidence of syncretism being widespread across religious traditions.
