Hadda, Afghanistan.fact: There were also five Roman gold solidi: Theodosius II (408–50 CE), Marcianus (450–457 CE) and Leo I (457–474 CE).

Hadda, Afghanistan.subject: Ancient India
Hadda, Afghanistan.question: Many coins were also _____ imitations of Sasanian coins with the addition of the Alkhon tamgha, and 14 Alkhon coins with rulers showing of their characteristic elongated skulls
Hadda, Afghanistan.fact: Many coins were also Hunnic imitations of Sasanian coins with the addition of the Alkhon tamgha, and 14 Alkhon coins with rulers showing of their characteristic elongated skulls.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The _____ was Roman emperor from 117 to 138.
Hadrian.fact: Hadrian ( HAY-dree-ən; born Publius Aelius Hadrianus, 24 January 76 – 10 July 138) was Roman emperor from 117 to 138. His form of address as Roman emperor was Imperator Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He was a member of the Nerva–_____ dynasty
Hadrian.fact: He was a member of the Nerva–Antonine dynasty.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He earned further disapproval by abandoning _____'s expansionist policies and territorial gains in Mesopotamia, Assyria, Armenia, and parts of Dacia
Hadrian.fact: Early in his political career, Hadrian married Vibia Sabina, grandniece of the ruling emperor, Trajan, and his second cousin once removed. The marriage and Hadrian's later succession as emperor were probably promoted by Trajan's wife Pompeia Plotina.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He visited almost every province of the _____, and indulged a preference for direct intervention in imperial and provincial affairs, especially building projects
Hadrian.fact: Hadrian preferred to invest in the development of stable, defensible borders and the unification of the Roman empire's disparate peoples and subjects. He visited almost every province of the Empire, and indulged a preference for direct intervention in imperial and provincial affairs, especially building projects.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: In Rome itself, he rebuilt the _____ and constructed the vast Temple of Venus and Roma, as well as the Villa Adriana in Tivoli
Hadrian.fact: In Rome itself, he rebuilt the Pantheon and constructed the vast Temple of Venus and Roma, as well as the Villa Adriana in Tivoli.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: In Egypt, he may have rebuilt the _____ of Alexandria
Hadrian.fact: In Egypt, he may have rebuilt the Serapeum of Alexandria.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: As an ardent admirer of Greek culture, he promoted _____ as the cultural capital of the Empire
Hadrian.fact: As an ardent admirer of Greek culture, he promoted Athens as the cultural capital of the Empire.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: In 138, he adopted _____ and nominated him as a successor, on condition that Antoninus adopt Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus as his own heirs
Hadrian.fact: In 138, he adopted Antoninus Pius and nominated him as a successor, on condition that Antoninus adopt Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus as his own heirs.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Later historians counted him as one of Rome's so-called "_____", and as a benevolent autocrat
Hadrian.fact: Later historians counted him as one of Rome's so-called "Five Good Emperors", and as a benevolent autocrat.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: His own _____ found him remote and authoritarian
Hadrian.fact: Hadrian died the same year at Baiae, and Antoninus had him deified, despite opposition from the Senate. His own Senate found him remote and authoritarian.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: His only sibling was an elder sister, _____
Hadrian.fact: His only sibling was an elder sister, Aelia Domitia Paulina.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: His wet nurse was the slave _____, probably of Germanic origin, to whom he was devoted throughout his life
Hadrian.fact: His wet nurse was the slave Germana, probably of Germanic origin, to whom he was devoted throughout his life.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: One author has proposed to consider them part of the "Ulpio-_____ dynasty"
Hadrian.fact: One author has proposed to consider them part of the "Ulpio-Aelian dynasty".

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He and his sister became wards of Trajan and _____ (who later became Trajan's Praetorian prefect)
Hadrian.fact: He and his sister became wards of Trajan and Publius Acilius Attianus (who later became Trajan's Praetorian prefect).

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He then served as a military tribune, first with the Legio II _____ in 95, then with the Legio V Macedonica
Hadrian.fact: He then served as a military tribune, first with the Legio II Adiutrix in 95, then with the Legio V Macedonica.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: His next post was as ab actis senatus, keeping the _____'s records
Hadrian.fact: In 101, Hadrian was back in Rome; he was elected quaestor, then quaestor imperatoris Traiani, liaison officer between Emperor and the assembled Senate, to whom he read the Emperor's communiqués and speeches – which he possibly composed on the emperor's behalf. His next post was as ab actis senatus, keeping the Senate's records.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He was released to serve as legate of Legio I _____, then as governor of Lower Pannonia in 107, tasked with "holding back the Sarmatians"
Hadrian.fact: He was released to serve as legate of Legio I Minervia, then as governor of Lower Pannonia in 107, tasked with "holding back the Sarmatians".

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: It is believed the _____ kept Oltenia in exchange for some form of concession, likely involving a one-time tribute payment
Hadrian.fact: It is believed the Romans kept Oltenia in exchange for some form of concession, likely involving a one-time tribute payment.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The Iazyges also took possession of _____ around this time, which may have been part of the treaty
Hadrian.fact: Between 107 and 108, Hadrian defeated an invasion of Roman-controlled Banat and Oltenia by the Iazyges. The Iazyges also took possession of Banat around this time, which may have been part of the treaty.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The Athenians awarded him a statue with an inscription in the _____ of Dionysus (IG II2 3286) offering a detailed account of his cursus honorum thus far
Hadrian.fact: The Athenians awarded him a statue with an inscription in the Theatre of Dionysus (IG II2 3286) offering a detailed account of his cursus honorum thus far.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Thereafter, no more is heard of him until Trajan's _____ campaign
Hadrian.fact: Thereafter, no more is heard of him until Trajan's Parthian campaign.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: It is possible that he remained in _____ until his recall to the imperial retinue, when he joined Trajan's expedition against Parthia as a legate
Hadrian.fact: Now in his mid-thirties, Hadrian travelled to Greece; he was granted Athenian citizenship and was appointed eponymous archon of Athens for a brief time (in 112). It is possible that he remained in Greece until his recall to the imperial retinue, when he joined Trajan's expedition against Parthia as a legate.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Trajan got as far as the coastal city of _____, in Cilicia, and died there on 8 August 117; he would be regarded as one of Rome's most admired, popular and best emperors
Hadrian.fact: Trajan got as far as the coastal city of Selinus, in Cilicia, and died there on 8 August 117; he would be regarded as one of Rome's most admired, popular and best emperors.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The marriage might have been arranged by Trajan's empress, _____
Hadrian.fact: The marriage might have been arranged by Trajan's empress, Plotina. If Hadrian were to be appointed Trajan's successor, Plotina and her extended family could retain their social profile and political influence after Trajan's death.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: When Ulpia Marciana died in 112, Trajan had her deified, and made _____ an Augusta
Hadrian.fact: Hadrian could also count on the support of his mother-in-law, Salonia Matidia, who was the daughter of Trajan's beloved sister Ulpia Marciana. When Ulpia Marciana died in 112, Trajan had her deified, and made Salonia Matidia an Augusta.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: It has been suggested that _____'s young manservant Phaedimus, who died very soon after Trajan, was killed (or killed himself) rather than face awkward questions
Hadrian.fact: As Trajan lay dying, nursed by his wife, Plotina, and closely watched by Prefect Attianus, he could have lawfully adopted Hadrian as heir by means of a simple deathbed wish, expressed before witnesses; but when an adoption document was eventually presented, it was signed not by Trajan but by Plotina. It has been suggested that Trajan's young manservant Phaedimus, who died very soon after Trajan, was killed (or killed himself) rather than face awkward questions.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The new emperor rewarded the legions' loyalty with the customary bonus, and the _____ endorsed the acclamation
Hadrian.fact: The new emperor rewarded the legions' loyalty with the customary bonus, and the Senate endorsed the acclamation.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He relieved Judea's governor, the outstanding Moorish general _____, of his personal guard of Moorish auxiliaries; then he moved on to quell disturbances along the Danube frontier
Hadrian.fact: He relieved Judea's governor, the outstanding Moorish general Lusius Quietus, of his personal guard of Moorish auxiliaries; then he moved on to quell disturbances along the Danube frontier. In Rome, Hadrian's former guardian and current praetorian prefect, Attianus, claimed to have uncovered a conspiracy involving Lusius Quietus and three other leading senators, Lucius Publilius Celsus, Aulus Cornelius Palma Frontonianus and Gaius Avidius Nigrinus.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: One of their number was _____ who as a former conqueror of Arabia Nabatea would have retained a stake in the East
Hadrian.fact: One of their number was Aulus Cornelius Palma who as a former conqueror of Arabia Nabatea would have retained a stake in the East.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Previous emperors had often left _____ for long periods, but mostly to go to war, returning once the conflict was settled
Hadrian.fact: Previous emperors had often left Rome for long periods, but mostly to go to war, returning once the conflict was settled.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He supported the creation of provincial towns (municipia), semi-autonomous urban communities with their own customs and laws, rather than the imposition of new _____ colonies with Roman constitutions
Hadrian.fact: Hadrian's near-incessant travels may represent a calculated break with traditions and attitudes in which the empire was a purely Roman hegemony. Hadrian sought to include provincials in a commonwealth of civilised peoples and a common Hellenic culture under Roman supervision.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: All this did not go well with _____ traditionalists
Hadrian.fact: Hadrian sought to include provincials in a commonwealth of civilised peoples and a common Hellenic culture under Roman supervision. He supported the creation of provincial towns (municipia), semi-autonomous urban communities with their own customs and laws, rather than the imposition of new Roman colonies with Roman constitutions.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The self-indulgent emperor Nero had enjoyed a prolonged and peaceful tour of _____ and had been criticised by the Roman elite for abandoning his fundamental responsibilities as emperor
Hadrian.fact: The self-indulgent emperor Nero had enjoyed a prolonged and peaceful tour of Greece and had been criticised by the Roman elite for abandoning his fundamental responsibilities as emperor.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: In the eastern provinces, and to some extent in the west, _____ had enjoyed popular support; claims of his imminent return or rebirth emerged almost immediately after his death
Hadrian.fact: The self-indulgent emperor Nero had enjoyed a prolonged and peaceful tour of Greece and had been criticised by the Roman elite for abandoning his fundamental responsibilities as emperor. In the eastern provinces, and to some extent in the west, Nero had enjoyed popular support; claims of his imminent return or rebirth emerged almost immediately after his death.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Inscriptions tell of an expeditio _____ that involved major troop movements, including the dispatch of a detachment (vexillatio), comprising some 3,000 soldiers
Hadrian.fact: Inscriptions tell of an expeditio Britannica that involved major troop movements, including the dispatch of a detachment (vexillatio), comprising some 3,000 soldiers.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Fronto writes about military losses in _____ at the time
Hadrian.fact: Fronto writes about military losses in Britannia at the time.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Coin legends of 119–120 attest that _____ was sent to restore order
Hadrian.fact: Coin legends of 119–120 attest that Quintus Pompeius Falco was sent to restore order.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: A general desire to cease the _____'s extension may have been the determining motive
Hadrian.fact: A general desire to cease the Empire's extension may have been the determining motive.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Reduction of defence costs may also have played a role, as the _____ deterred attacks on Roman territory at a lower cost than a massed border army, and controlled cross-border trade and immigration
Hadrian.fact: In 122 Hadrian initiated the construction of a wall "to separate Romans from barbarians". The idea that the wall was built in order to deal with an actual threat or its resurgence, however, is probable but nevertheless conjectural.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: A shrine was erected in York to _____ as the divine personification of Britain; coins were struck, bearing her image, identified as Britannia
Hadrian.fact: A shrine was erected in York to Britannia as the divine personification of Britain; coins were struck, bearing her image, identified as Britannia. By the end of 122, Hadrian had concluded his visit to Britannia.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: At some point, he visited _____, where he personally funded the training of young men from well-bred families for the Roman military
Hadrian.fact: At some point, he visited Cyrene, where he personally funded the training of young men from well-bred families for the Roman military. Cyrene had benefited earlier in Hadrian's reign (in 119) from his restoration of public buildings destroyed during the earlier, Trajanic Jewish revolt.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He probably wintered in _____, the main city of Bithynia
Hadrian.fact: He probably wintered in Nicomedia, the main city of Bithynia. Nicomedia had been hit by an earthquake only shortly before his stay; Hadrian provided funds for its rebuilding and was acclaimed as restorer of the province.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Literary and epigraphic sources say nothing of when or where they met; depictions of _____ show him aged 20 or so, shortly before his death in 130
Hadrian.fact: It is possible that Hadrian visited Claudiopolis and saw the beautiful Antinous, a young man of humble birth who became Hadrian's lover. Literary and epigraphic sources say nothing of when or where they met; depictions of Antinous show him aged 20 or so, shortly before his death in 130.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: It is also possible that _____ was sent to Rome to be trained as a page to serve the emperor and only gradually rose to the status of imperial favourite
Hadrian.fact: It is possible that Hadrian visited Claudiopolis and saw the beautiful Antinous, a young man of humble birth who became Hadrian's lover. Literary and epigraphic sources say nothing of when or where they met; depictions of Antinous show him aged 20 or so, shortly before his death in 130.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: At about this time, plans to complete the Temple of Zeus in _____, begun by the kings of Pergamon, were put into practice
Hadrian.fact: At about this time, plans to complete the Temple of Zeus in Cyzicus, begun by the kings of Pergamon, were put into practice. Cyzicus, Pergamon, Smyrna, Ephesus and Sardes were promoted as regional centres for the imperial cult (neocoros).

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Cyzicus, _____, Smyrna, Ephesus and Sardes were promoted as regional centres for the imperial cult (neocoros)
Hadrian.fact: At about this time, plans to complete the Temple of Zeus in Cyzicus, begun by the kings of Pergamon, were put into practice. Cyzicus, Pergamon, Smyrna, Ephesus and Sardes were promoted as regional centres for the imperial cult (neocoros).

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Several were given to Argos, to remedy a water-shortage so severe and so long-standing that "thirsty Argos" featured in _____ epic
Hadrian.fact: Several were given to Argos, to remedy a water-shortage so severe and so long-standing that "thirsty Argos" featured in Homeric epic.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He restored _____'s Temple of Poseidon Hippios, and according to Pausanias, restored the city's original, classical name
Hadrian.fact: Antinous and Hadrian may have already been lovers at this time; Hadrian showed particular generosity to Mantinea, which shared ancient, mythic, politically useful links with Antinous' home at Bithynia. He restored Mantinea's Temple of Poseidon Hippios, and according to Pausanias, restored the city's original, classical name.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: It had been renamed _____ since Hellenistic times, after the Macedonian King Antigonus III Doson
Hadrian.fact: It had been renamed Antigoneia since Hellenistic times, after the Macedonian King Antigonus III Doson.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The two aristocrats would be the first from "_____" to enter the Roman Senate, as representatives of Sparta and Athens, traditional rivals and "great powers" of the Classical Age
Hadrian.fact: The two aristocrats would be the first from "Old Greece" to enter the Roman Senate, as representatives of Sparta and Athens, traditional rivals and "great powers" of the Classical Age.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: This was an important step in overcoming _____ notables' reluctance to take part in Roman political life
Hadrian.fact: This was an important step in overcoming Greek notables' reluctance to take part in Roman political life.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Back in Rome, he saw the rebuilt _____ and his completed villa at nearby Tibur, among the Sabine Hills
Hadrian.fact: Back in Rome, he saw the rebuilt Pantheon and his completed villa at nearby Tibur, among the Sabine Hills.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He restored the shrine of Cupra in _____ and improved the drainage of the Fucine lake
Hadrian.fact: He restored the shrine of Cupra in Cupra Maritima and improved the drainage of the Fucine lake.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Less welcome than such largesse was his decision in 127 to divide _____ into four regions under imperial legates with consular rank, acting as governors
Hadrian.fact: In early March 127 Hadrian set off on a tour of Italy; his route has been reconstructed through the evidence of his gifts and donations. Less welcome than such largesse was his decision in 127 to divide Italy into four regions under imperial legates with consular rank, acting as governors.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: They were given jurisdiction over all of Italy, excluding Rome itself, therefore shifting _____ cases from the courts of Rome
Hadrian.fact: They were given jurisdiction over all of Italy, excluding Rome itself, therefore shifting Italian cases from the courts of Rome.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: This time his visit to _____ seems to have concentrated on Athens and Sparta – the two ancient rivals for dominance of Greece
Hadrian.fact: This time his visit to Greece seems to have concentrated on Athens and Sparta – the two ancient rivals for dominance of Greece.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: His new _____ was going to be a council that would bring Greek cities together
Hadrian.fact: His new Panhellenion was going to be a council that would bring Greek cities together.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He opened his stay in Egypt by restoring Pompey the Great's tomb at _____, offering sacrifice to him as a hero and composing an epigraph for the tomb
Hadrian.fact: He opened his stay in Egypt by restoring Pompey the Great's tomb at Pelusium, offering sacrifice to him as a hero and composing an epigraph for the tomb.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Historia Augusta offers the following account: During a journey on the Nile he lost _____, his favourite, and for this youth he wept like a woman
Hadrian.fact: Hadrian and Antinous held a lion hunt in the Libyan desert; a poem on the subject by the Greek Pankrates is the earliest evidence that they travelled together. While Hadrian and his entourage were sailing on the Nile, Antinous drowned.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He then continued down the Nile to Thebes, where his visit to the _____ of Memnon on 20 and 21 November was commemorated by four epigrams inscribed by Julia Balbilla
Hadrian.fact: He then continued down the Nile to Thebes, where his visit to the Colossi of Memnon on 20 and 21 November was commemorated by four epigrams inscribed by Julia Balbilla.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: After that, he headed north, reaching the Fayyum at the beginning of _____
Hadrian.fact: After that, he headed north, reaching the Fayyum at the beginning of December.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Whether or not he returned to Rome, he travelled in the East during 130–131, to organise and inaugurate his new _____, which was to be focused on the Athenian Temple to Olympian Zeus
Hadrian.fact: Whether or not he returned to Rome, he travelled in the East during 130–131, to organise and inaugurate his new Panhellenion, which was to be focused on the Athenian Temple to Olympian Zeus.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Some cities with a dubious claim to _____, however – such as Side – were acknowledged as fully Hellenic
Hadrian.fact: Hadrian's notion of Hellenism was narrow and deliberately archaising; he defined "Greekness" in terms of classical roots, rather than a broader, Hellenistic culture. Some cities with a dubious claim to Greekness, however – such as Side – were acknowledged as fully Hellenic.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The German sociologist _____ remarked that the Panhellenion was based on "games, commemorations, preservation of an ideal, an entirely non-political Hellenism"
Hadrian.fact: The German sociologist Georg Simmel remarked that the Panhellenion was based on "games, commemorations, preservation of an ideal, an entirely non-political Hellenism".

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He may have planned to rebuild _____ as a colonia as Vespasian had done with Caesarea Maritima – with various honorific and fiscal privileges
Hadrian.fact: He may have planned to rebuild Jerusalem as a colonia as Vespasian had done with Caesarea Maritima – with various honorific and fiscal privileges. It has been speculated that Hadrian intended to assimilate the Temple in Jerusalem to the traditional civic-religious Roman imperial cult; such assimilations had long been commonplace practice in Greece and in other provinces, and on the whole, had been successful.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The Samaritans had already integrated their religious rites with _____ ones
Hadrian.fact: The Samaritans had already integrated their religious rites with Hellenistic ones.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The Roman governor _____ (Tynius) Rufus asked for an army to crush the resistance; bar Kokhba punished any Jew who refused to join his ranks
Hadrian.fact: The Roman governor Tineius (Tynius) Rufus asked for an army to crush the resistance; bar Kokhba punished any Jew who refused to join his ranks.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: According to _____ and Eusebius, that had to do mostly with Christian converts, who opposed bar Kokhba's messianic claims
Hadrian.fact: According to Justin Martyr and Eusebius, that had to do mostly with Christian converts, who opposed bar Kokhba's messianic claims.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Beitar, a fortified city _____ (6.2 mi) southwest of Jerusalem, fell after a three-and-a-half-year siege
Hadrian.fact: Beitar, a fortified city 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) southwest of Jerusalem, fell after a three-and-a-half-year siege.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The extent of punitive measures against the _____ population remains a matter of debate
Hadrian.fact: The extent of punitive measures against the Jewish population remains a matter of debate.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He renamed _____ after himself and Jupiter Capitolinus and had the city rebuilt in Greek style
Hadrian.fact: He renamed Jerusalem Aelia Capitolina after himself and Jupiter Capitolinus and had the city rebuilt in Greek style.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: The bloody repression of the revolt ended _____ political independence from the Roman imperial order
Hadrian.fact: After the suppression of the Jewish revolt, Hadrian provided the Samaritans with a temple dedicated to Zeus Hypsistos ("Highest Zeus") on Mount Gerizim. The bloody repression of the revolt ended Jewish political independence from the Roman imperial order.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He then returned to Rome, probably in that year and almost certainly – judging from inscriptions – via _____
Hadrian.fact: He then returned to Rome, probably in that year and almost certainly – judging from inscriptions – via Illyricum.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: In 134, he took an imperial salutation for the end of the _____ (which was not actually concluded until the following year)
Hadrian.fact: In 134, he took an imperial salutation for the end of the Third Jewish War (which was not actually concluded until the following year).

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: In keeping with well-established imperial propriety, Sabina – who had been made an _____ sometime around 128 – was deified not long after her death
Hadrian.fact: The Historia Augusta biography states that Hadrian himself declared that his wife's "ill-temper and irritability" would be reason enough for a divorce, were he a private citizen. In keeping with well-established imperial propriety, Sabina – who had been made an Augusta sometime around 128 – was deified not long after her death.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: In 136, he adopted one of the ordinary consuls of that year, _____, who, as an emperor-in-waiting, took the name Lucius Aelius Caesar
Hadrian.fact: In 136, he adopted one of the ordinary consuls of that year, Lucius Ceionius Commodus, who, as an emperor-in-waiting, took the name Lucius Aelius Caesar.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He was the son-in-law of _____, one of the "four consulars" executed in 118
Hadrian.fact: He was the son-in-law of Gaius Avidius Nigrinus, one of the "four consulars" executed in 118.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Aelius acquitted himself honourably as joint governor of _____ and Pannonia Inferior; he held a further consulship in 137 but died on 1 January 138
Hadrian.fact: Aelius acquitted himself honourably as joint governor of Pannonia Superior and Pannonia Inferior; he held a further consulship in 137 but died on 1 January 138.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: When he eventually became _____, Marcus Aurelius would co-opt Ceionius Commodus as his co-Emperor, under the name of Lucius Verus, on his own initiative
Hadrian.fact: Hadrian next adopted Titus Aurelius Fulvus Boionius Arrius Antoninus (the future emperor Antoninus Pius), who had served Hadrian as one of the five imperial legates of Italy, and as proconsul of Asia. When he eventually became Emperor, Marcus Aurelius would co-opt Ceionius Commodus as his co-Emperor, under the name of Lucius Verus, on his own initiative.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: He was buried at _____, near Baiae, on an estate that had once belonged to Cicero
Hadrian.fact: He was buried at Puteoli, near Baiae, on an estate that had once belonged to Cicero.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Soon after, his remains were transferred to Rome and buried in the _____ of Domitia, close to the almost-complete mausoleum
Hadrian.fact: Soon after, his remains were transferred to Rome and buried in the Gardens of Domitia, close to the almost-complete mausoleum.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: His ashes were placed there together with those of his wife Vibia Sabina and his first adopted son, Lucius Aelius Caesar, who also died in _____
Hadrian.fact: His ashes were placed there together with those of his wife Vibia Sabina and his first adopted son, Lucius Aelius Caesar, who also died in 138.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Trajan himself may have thought his gains in _____ indefensible and abandoned them shortly before his death
Hadrian.fact: The 4th-century historian Aurelius Victor saw Hadrian's withdrawal from Trajan's territorial gains in Mesopotamia as a jealous belittlement of Trajan's achievements (Traiani gloriae invidens). Trajan himself may have thought his gains in Mesopotamia indefensible and abandoned them shortly before his death.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: A controlled partial withdrawal of troops from the _____ plains would have been less costly than maintaining several Roman cavalry units and a supporting network of fortifications
Hadrian.fact: Hadrian's presence on the Dacian front is mere conjecture, but Dacia was included in his coin series with allegories of the provinces. A controlled partial withdrawal of troops from the Dacian plains would have been less costly than maintaining several Roman cavalry units and a supporting network of fortifications.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: Late in his reign (135), the Alani attacked _____ with the covert support of Pharasmanes, the king of Caucasian Iberia
Hadrian.fact: Late in his reign (135), the Alani attacked Roman Cappadocia with the covert support of Pharasmanes, the king of Caucasian Iberia.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: That helped keep the military usefully occupied in times of peace; his wall across _____ was built by ordinary troops
Hadrian.fact: That helped keep the military usefully occupied in times of peace; his wall across Britannia was built by ordinary troops.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: A series of mostly wooden fortifications, forts, outposts and watchtowers strengthened the _____ and Rhine borders
Hadrian.fact: A series of mostly wooden fortifications, forts, outposts and watchtowers strengthened the Danube and Rhine borders.

Hadrian.subject: Ancient India
Hadrian.question: This innovation marked the superseding of surviving _____ institutions by an openly autocratic political system
Hadrian.fact: This innovation marked the superseding of surviving Republican institutions by an openly autocratic political system.

Hannibal.fact: The only alternative route to central Italy lay at the mouth of the Arno. Hannibal knew that this route was full of difficulties, but it remained the surest and quickest way to central Italy.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: He arrived in _____ in the spring of 217 BC and decided to lure the main Roman army under Flaminius into a pitched battle by devastating the region that Flaminius had been sent to protect
Hannibal.fact: He arrived in Etruria in the spring of 217 BC and decided to lure the main Roman army under Flaminius into a pitched battle by devastating the region that Flaminius had been sent to protect.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Despite this, _____ remained passively encamped at Arretium
Hannibal.fact: He arrived in Etruria in the spring of 217 BC and decided to lure the main Roman army under Flaminius into a pitched battle by devastating the region that Flaminius had been sent to protect. As Polybius recounts, "he [Hannibal] calculated that, if he passed the camp and made a descent into the district beyond, Flaminius (partly for fear of popular reproach and partly of personal irritation) would be unable to endure watching passively the devastation of the country but would spontaneously fol...

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: He then advanced through the uplands of _____, provoking Flaminius into a hasty pursuit and catching him in a defile on the shore of Lake Trasimenus
Hannibal.fact: He then advanced through the uplands of Etruria, provoking Flaminius into a hasty pursuit and catching him in a defile on the shore of Lake Trasimenus.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: This was the most costly ambush that the Romans ever sustained until the Battle of _____ in 53 BC
Hannibal.fact: This was the most costly ambush that the Romans ever sustained until the Battle of Carrhae in 53 BC.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: He opted to exploit his victory by entering into central and southern _____ and encouraging a general revolt against the sovereign power
Hannibal.fact: He opted to exploit his victory by entering into central and southern Italy and encouraging a general revolt against the sovereign power. Hannibal ravaged Apulia but was unable to bring Fabius to battle, so he decided to march through Samnium to Campania, one of the richest and most fertile provinces of Italy, hoping that the devastation would draw Fabius into battle.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The Romans appointed _____ as their dictator
Hannibal.fact: The Romans appointed Quintus Fabius Maximus Verrucosus as their dictator.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: This strategy was unpopular with many _____, who believed that it was a form of cowardice
Hannibal.fact: This strategy was unpopular with many Romans, who believed that it was a form of cowardice.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: This situation led to the night Battle of _____
Hannibal.fact: This situation led to the night Battle of Ager Falernus.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Some of the _____, seeing a moving column of lights, were tricked into believing it was the Carthaginian army marching to escape along the heights
Hannibal.fact: Some of the Romans, seeing a moving column of lights, were tricked into believing it was the Carthaginian army marching to escape along the heights.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: This was a severe blow to _____' prestige, and when his dictatorial term ended soon after, it was not renewed
Hannibal.fact: Fabius was within striking distance, but in this case his caution worked against him, as rightly sensing a trick he stayed put. This was a severe blow to Fabius' prestige, and when his dictatorial term ended soon after, it was not renewed.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Once the _____ resumed their consular elections in 216 BC, they appointed Gaius Terentius Varro and Lucius Aemilius Paullus as consuls
Hannibal.fact: Once the Roman Senate resumed their consular elections in 216 BC, they appointed Gaius Terentius Varro and Lucius Aemilius Paullus as consuls.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: They eventually found him on the left bank of the _____ and encamped 10 km (6 mi) away
Hannibal.fact: They eventually found him on the left bank of the Aufidus River and encamped 10 km (6 mi) away.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: According to _____, Varro was a man of reckless and hubristic nature, and it was his turn to command on the day of battle
Hannibal.fact: According to Livy, Varro was a man of reckless and hubristic nature, and it was his turn to command on the day of battle.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: This account is possibly biased against Varro as its main source, _____, was a client of Paullus's aristocratic family whereas Varro was less distinguished
Hannibal.fact: This account is possibly biased against Varro as its main source, Polybius, was a client of Paullus's aristocratic family whereas Varro was less distinguished.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: This theory is supported by the fact that after Varro survived the battle he was pardoned by the _____, which would be peculiar if he were the sole commander at fault
Hannibal.fact: This theory is supported by the fact that after Varro survived the battle he was pardoned by the Senate, which would be peculiar if he were the sole commander at fault.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: This eliminated the _____ numerical advantage by shrinking the combat area
Hannibal.fact: Hannibal capitalized on the eagerness of the Romans and drew them into a trap by using an envelopment tactic. This eliminated the Roman numerical advantage by shrinking the combat area.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Placing them forward of the wings allowed them room to fall back, luring the _____ after them, while the cavalry on the flanks dealt with their Roman counterparts
Hannibal.fact: Hannibal capitalized on the eagerness of the Romans and drew them into a trap by using an envelopment tactic. Hannibal drew up his least reliable infantry in the centre in a semicircle curving towards the Romans.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: As a result, the _____ army was fully surrounded with no means of escape
Hannibal.fact: Hannibal's chief cavalry commander Maharbal led the mobile Numidian cavalry on the right which shattered the Roman cavalry opposing them. Hannibal's Iberian and Gallic heavy cavalry on the left, led by Hanno, defeated the Roman heavy cavalry after which both the Carthaginian heavy cavalry and the Numidians attacked the legions from behind.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Depending upon the source, it is estimated that 50,000–70,000 _____ were killed or captured
Hannibal.fact: Depending upon the source, it is estimated that 50,000–70,000 Romans were killed or captured.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Among the dead were _____, two consuls for the preceding year, two quaestors, 29 of the 48 military tribunes, and an additional 80 senators
Hannibal.fact: Among the dead were Roman Consul Lucius Aemilius Paullus, two consuls for the preceding year, two quaestors, 29 of the 48 military tribunes, and an additional 80 senators.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: At a time when the _____ was composed of no more than 300 men, this constituted 25–30% of the governing body
Hannibal.fact: At a time when the Roman Senate was composed of no more than 300 men, this constituted 25–30% of the governing body.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: It is believed that his refusal to bring the war to Rome was a lack of commitment from _____ of men, money, and material—principally siege equipment
Hannibal.fact: It is believed that his refusal to bring the war to Rome was a lack of commitment from Carthage of men, money, and material—principally siege equipment.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: However, only a few of the _____ city-states that he had expected to gain as allies defected to him
Hannibal.fact: Instead, he had to content himself with subduing the fortresses that still held out against him, and the only other notable event of 216 BC was the defection of certain Italian territories, including Capua, the second largest city of Italy, which Hannibal made his base. However, only a few of the Italian city-states that he had expected to gain as allies defected to him.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Although Phoenician territories like Tyre and Sidon possessed the necessary combination of raw materials, technical expertise, and _____, it took much longer than expected for it to be completed, most likely due to wartime shortages
Hannibal.fact: Although Phoenician territories like Tyre and Sidon possessed the necessary combination of raw materials, technical expertise, and experienced personnel, it took much longer than expected for it to be completed, most likely due to wartime shortages.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: His immediate objectives were reduced to minor operations centred mainly around the cities of _____
Hannibal.fact: His immediate objectives were reduced to minor operations centred mainly around the cities of Campania.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The forces detached to his lieutenants were generally unable to hold their own, and neither his home government nor _____ V helped to make up his losses
Hannibal.fact: The forces detached to his lieutenants were generally unable to hold their own, and neither his home government nor Philip V helped to make up his losses.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: His position in southern _____ therefore became increasingly difficult, and his chance of ultimately conquering Rome grew ever more remote
Hannibal.fact: For the next few years, Hannibal was forced to sustain a scorched earth policy and obtain local provisions for protracted and ineffectual operations throughout southern Italy. His position in southern Italy therefore became increasingly difficult, and his chance of ultimately conquering Rome grew ever more remote.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: There was a _____, but the real power was with the inner "Council of 30 Nobles" and the board of judges from ruling families known as the "Hundred and Four"
Hannibal.fact: There was a Carthaginian Senate, but the real power was with the inner "Council of 30 Nobles" and the board of judges from ruling families called the "Hundred and Four".

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The tide was slowly turning against him and in favor of _____
Hannibal.fact: He and his allies relied on trade with Rome to sustain their wealth and resented how Hannibal's unauthorized attack of Saguntum had forced them to choose between losing prestige or committing Carthage to war. Thus, they repeatedly acted to thwart Hannibal's plans; requests for supplies and equipment that would have made besieging Rome and its fortified cities possible were either delayed or ignored, and Carthaginian soldiers in northern Africa were not sent to reinforce Hannibal, forcing him ...

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The Roman consuls mounted a siege of _____ in 212 BC
Hannibal.fact: The Roman consuls mounted a siege of Capua in 212 BC.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: He moved to _____ and destroyed a 16,000-man Roman army at the Battle of the Silarus, with 15,000 Romans killed
Hannibal.fact: He moved to Lucania and destroyed a 16,000-man Roman army at the Battle of the Silarus, with 15,000 Romans killed.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Another opportunity presented itself soon after, a Roman army of _____ men being destroyed by Hannibal at the first battle of Herdonia with 16,000 Romans dead, freeing Apulia from the Romans for the y
Hannibal.fact: Another opportunity presented itself soon after, a Roman army of 18,000 men being destroyed by Hannibal at the first battle of Herdonia with 16,000 Romans dead, freeing Apulia from the Romans for the year.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The Roman consuls mounted another siege of _____ in 211 BC, conquering the city
Hannibal.fact: The Roman consuls mounted another siege of Capua in 211 BC, conquering the city. He drew off 15,000 Roman soldiers, but the siege continued, and Capua fell.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: He marched on _____ to force the recall of the Roman armies
Hannibal.fact: He marched on Rome to force the recall of the Roman armies. In 210 BC, the Romans entered into an alliance with the Aetolian League to counter Philip V. Philip, who attempted to exploit Rome's preoccupation in Italy to conquer Illyria, found himself under attack from several sides at once and was quickly subdued by Rome and her Greek allies.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: He drew off 15,000 _____ soldiers, but the siege continued, and Capua fell
Hannibal.fact: The Roman consuls mounted another siege of Capua in 211 BC, conquering the city. Hannibal's attempt to lift the siege with an assault on the Roman siege lines failed.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: In 212 BC _____ conquered Syracuse, and the Romans destroyed the Carthaginian army in Sicily in 211–210 BC
Hannibal.fact: In 212 BC Marcellus conquered Syracuse, and the Romans destroyed the Carthaginian army in Sicily in 211–210 BC.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: But with the loss of _____ in 209 BC and the gradual reconquest by the Romans of Samnium and Lucania, his hold on south Italy was almost lost
Hannibal.fact: But with the loss of Tarentum in 209 BC and the gradual reconquest by the Romans of Samnium and Lucania, his hold on south Italy was almost lost.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: In 207 BC he succeeded in making his way again into _____, where he waited to concert measures for a combined march upon Rome with his brother Hasdrubal
Hannibal.fact: In 210 BC Hannibal again proved his superiority in tactics by inflicting a severe defeat at the Battle of Herdonia in Apulia upon a proconsular army and, in 208 BC he destroyed a Roman force engaged in the siege of Locri at the Battle of Petelia. In 207 BC he succeeded in making his way again into Apulia, where he waited to concert measures for a combined march upon Rome with his brother Hasdrubal.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: On hearing of _____'s defeat and death at the Battle of the Metaurus he retired to Calabria, where he maintained himself for the ensuing years
Hannibal.fact: In 207 BC he succeeded in making his way again into Apulia, where he waited to concert measures for a combined march upon Rome with his brother Hasdrubal. On hearing of Hasdrubal's defeat and death at the Battle of the Metaurus he retired to Calabria, where he maintained himself for the ensuing years.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: With the failure of his brother Mago in _____ (205–203 BC) and of his own negotiations with Phillip, the last hope of recovering his ascendancy in Italy was lost
Hannibal.fact: With the failure of his brother Mago in Liguria (205–203 BC) and of his own negotiations with Phillip, the last hope of recovering his ascendancy in Italy was lost.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: After leaving a record of his expedition engraved in Punic and Greek upon bronze tablets in the Temple of _____ at Crotona, he sailed back to Africa
Hannibal.fact: After leaving a record of his expedition engraved in Punic and Greek upon bronze tablets in the Temple of Juno Lacinia at Crotona, he sailed back to Africa.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: His arrival immediately restored the predominance of the war party, which placed him in command of a combined force of _____ levies and his mercenaries from Italy
Hannibal.fact: His arrival immediately restored the predominance of the war party, which placed him in command of a combined force of African levies and his mercenaries from Italy.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Scipio and _____ had worked out a peace plan, which was approved by Rome
Hannibal.fact: Scipio and Carthage had worked out a peace plan, which was approved by Rome. Carthage could keep its African territory but would lose its overseas empire.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The terms of the treaty were quite modest, but the war had been long for the _____
Hannibal.fact: The terms of the treaty were quite modest, but the war had been long for the Romans.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Carthage could keep its _____ territory but would lose its overseas empire
Hannibal.fact: Carthage could keep its African territory but would lose its overseas empire.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Also, _____ was to reduce its fleet and pay a war indemnity
Hannibal.fact: Carthage could keep its African territory but would lose its overseas empire. Also, Carthage was to reduce its fleet and pay a war indemnity.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Its long-suffering citizens had captured a stranded _____ fleet in the Gulf of Tunis and stripped it of supplies, an action that aggravated the faltering negotiations
Hannibal.fact: Its long-suffering citizens had captured a stranded Roman fleet in the Gulf of Tunis and stripped it of supplies, an action that aggravated the faltering negotiations. Fortified by both Hannibal and the supplies, the Carthaginians rebuffed the treaty and Roman protests.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The Roman cavalry won an early victory by swiftly routing the _____ cavalry
Hannibal.fact: Fortified by both Hannibal and the supplies, the Carthaginians rebuffed the treaty and Roman protests. This Roman cavalry superiority was due to the betrayal of King Masinissa of Numidia, who had earlier assisted Carthage in Iberia but changed sides in 206 BC with the promise of land, and due to his personal conflicts with Syphax, a Carthaginian ally.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The Romans were also successful in limiting the effectiveness of the war elephants with tactics such as playing trumpets to frighten the elephants and cause them to run into the _____ lines
Hannibal.fact: This Roman cavalry superiority was due to the betrayal of King Masinissa of Numidia, who had earlier assisted Carthage in Iberia but changed sides in 206 BC with the promise of land, and due to his personal conflicts with Syphax, a Carthaginian ally. Although the ageing Hannibal was suffering from mental exhaustion and deteriorating health after years of campaigning in Italy, the Carthaginians still had the advantage in numbers and were boosted by 80 war elephants.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: This two-pronged attack caused the _____ formation to collapse
Hannibal.fact: This two-pronged attack caused the Carthaginian formation to collapse. With their foremost general defeated, the Carthaginians had no choice but to surrender.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: With their foremost general defeated, the _____ had no choice but to surrender
Hannibal.fact: With their foremost general defeated, the Carthaginians had no choice but to surrender. The last major battle of the Second Punic War resulted in a loss of respect for Hannibal by his fellow Carthaginians.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The conditions of defeat were such that _____ could no longer battle for Mediterranean supremacy
Hannibal.fact: Carthage lost approximately 20,000 troops with an additional 15,000 wounded. The conditions of defeat were such that Carthage could no longer battle for Mediterranean supremacy.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Following the conclusion of a peace that left _____ saddled with an indemnity of ten thousand talents, he was elected suffete (chief magistrate) of the Carthaginian state
Hannibal.fact: The conditions of defeat were such that Carthage could no longer battle for Mediterranean supremacy. Following the conclusion of a peace that left Carthage saddled with an indemnity of ten thousand talents, he was elected suffete (chief magistrate) of the Carthaginian state.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The principal beneficiaries of these financial peculations had been the oligarchs of the _____ and Four
Hannibal.fact: The principal beneficiaries of these financial peculations had been the oligarchs of the Hundred and Four. In order to reduce their power, Hannibal passed a law stipulating the Hundred and Four be chosen by direct election rather than co-option.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: He also used citizen support to change the term of office in the _____ and Four from life to one year, with none permitted to hold office for two consecutive years
Hannibal.fact: The principal beneficiaries of these financial peculations had been the oligarchs of the Hundred and Four. In order to reduce their power, Hannibal passed a law stipulating the Hundred and Four be chosen by direct election rather than co-option.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: He journeyed first to Tyre, the mother city of _____, and then to Antioch, before he finally reached Ephesus where he was honourably received by Antiochus
Hannibal.fact: Aware that he had many enemies, not the least of which were because of his financial reforms eliminating corruption, Hannibal fled into voluntary exile before the Romans could demand that Carthage surrender him into their custody. He journeyed first to Tyre, the mother city of Carthage, and then to Antioch, before he finally reached Ephesus where he was honourably received by Antiochus.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: In _____ BC, after having suffered a series of defeats in the Roman–Seleucid war, Antiochus gave Hannibal his first significant military command after spending five years in the Seleucid court
Hannibal.fact: In 190 BC, after having suffered a series of defeats in the Roman–Seleucid war, Antiochus gave Hannibal his first significant military command after spending five years in the Seleucid court.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The ensuing Battle of _____ resulted in a Roman-Rhodian victory, which cemented Roman control over the Aegean Sea, enabling them to launch an invasion of Seleucid Asia Minor
Hannibal.fact: The ensuing Battle of Myonessus resulted in a Roman-Rhodian victory, which cemented Roman control over the Aegean Sea, enabling them to launch an invasion of Seleucid Asia Minor.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The two armies faced off in the Battle of _____, resulting in a decisive Roman-Pergamene victory
Hannibal.fact: The two armies faced off in the Battle of Magnesia, resulting in a decisive Roman-Pergamene victory.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: In 190 BC he gained a naval victory over _____ by throwing clay pots filled with venomous snakes onto Eumenes' ships
Hannibal.fact: Suspicious that Antiochus was prepared to surrender him to the Romans, Hannibal fled to Crete, but he soon went back to Anatolia and sought refuge with Prusias I of Bithynia, who was engaged in warfare with Rome's ally, King Eumenes II of Pergamon. In 190 BC he gained a naval victory over Eumenes by throwing clay pots filled with venomous snakes onto Eumenes' ships.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: According to some, _____ was sited at Gebze, between Bursa and Üskudar
Hannibal.fact: Pliny the Elder and Plutarch, in his Life of Flamininus, record that Hannibal's tomb was at Libyssa on the coast of the Sea of Marmara. According to some, Libyssa was sited at Gebze, between Bursa and Üskudar.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: W. M. Leake, identifying Gebze with ancient _____, places it further west
Hannibal.fact: W. M. Leake, identifying Gebze with ancient Dakibyza, places it further west.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: His legacy was recorded by his Greek tutor, _____ of Lacedaemon
Hannibal.fact: His legacy was recorded by his Greek tutor, Sosylus of Lacedaemon.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The works of Roman writers such as Livy (64 or 59 BC – AD 12 or 17), _____ (c
Hannibal.fact: The works of Roman writers such as Livy (64 or 59 BC – AD 12 or 17), Frontinus (c.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: The Romans even built statues of him in the streets of _____ to advertise their defeat of such a worthy adversary
Hannibal.fact: The Romans even built statues of him in the streets of Rome to advertise their defeat of such a worthy adversary. It is plausible to suggest that Hannibal engendered the greatest fear Rome had towards an enemy.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Nevertheless, the _____ grimly refused to admit the possibility of defeat and rejected all overtures for peace; they even refused to accept the ransom of prisoners after the Battle of Cannae
Hannibal.fact: The Romans even built statues of him in the streets of Rome to advertise their defeat of such a worthy adversary. Nevertheless, the Romans grimly refused to admit the possibility of defeat and rejected all overtures for peace; they even refused to accept the ransom of prisoners after the Battle of Cannae.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: During the war there are no reports of revolutions among the Roman citizens, no factions within the Senate desiring peace, no pro-_____ turncoats, and no coups
Hannibal.fact: During the war there are no reports of revolutions among the Roman citizens, no factions within the Senate desiring peace, no pro-Carthaginian Roman turncoats, and no coups.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Throughout the war, _____ aristocrats ferociously competed with each other for positions of command to fight against Rome's most dangerous enemy
Hannibal.fact: Nevertheless, the Romans grimly refused to admit the possibility of defeat and rejected all overtures for peace; they even refused to accept the ransom of prisoners after the Battle of Cannae. During the war there are no reports of revolutions among the Roman citizens, no factions within the Senate desiring peace, no pro-Carthaginian Roman turncoats, and no coups.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: In fact, they were reinforced and the campaigns there maintained until victory was secured; beginning first in Sicily under the direction of _____, and later in Hispania under Scipio Africanus
Hannibal.fact: In fact, they were reinforced and the campaigns there maintained until victory was secured; beginning first in Sicily under the direction of Claudius Marcellus, and later in Hispania under Scipio Africanus.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: They considered him the greatest enemy _____ had ever faced
Hannibal.fact: Although the long-term consequences of Hannibal's war are debatable, this war was undeniably Rome's "finest hour". They considered him the greatest enemy Rome had ever faced.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Any bias attributed to _____, however, is more troublesome
Hannibal.fact: Any bias attributed to Polybius, however, is more troublesome. Nonetheless, Polybius did recognize that the reputation for cruelty the Romans attached to Hannibal might in reality have been by mistaking him for one of his officers, Hannibal Monomachus.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: To this _____ assented since he also yielded the first place to Alexander
Hannibal.fact: According to Appian, several years after the Second Punic War, Hannibal served as a political advisor in the Seleucid Kingdom and Scipio arrived there on a diplomatic mission from Rome. It is said that at one of their meetings in the gymnasium Scipio and Hannibal had a conversation on the subject of generalship, in the presence of a number of bystanders, and that Scipio asked Hannibal whom he considered the greatest general, to which the latter replied "Alexander of Macedonia".

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Wonderful as his achievements were, we must marvel the more when we take into account the grudging support he received from _____
Hannibal.fact: Wonderful as his achievements were, we must marvel the more when we take into account the grudging support he received from Carthage.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: We never hear of a mutiny in his army, composed though it was of _____, Iberians and Gauls
Hannibal.fact: We never hear of a mutiny in his army, composed though it was of North Africans, Iberians and Gauls.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Livy speaks of his great qualities, but he adds that his vices were equally great, among which he singles out his more than _____ perfidy and an inhuman cruelty
Hannibal.fact: Livy speaks of his great qualities, but he adds that his vices were equally great, among which he singles out his more than Punic perfidy and an inhuman cruelty.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: No such brutality stains his name as that perpetrated by _____ on the vanquished Hasdrubal
Hannibal.fact: No such brutality stains his name as that perpetrated by Gaius Claudius Nero on the vanquished Hasdrubal.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Polybius merely says that he was accused of cruelty by the Romans and of avarice by the _____
Hannibal.fact: Polybius merely says that he was accused of cruelty by the Romans and of avarice by the Carthaginians.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: According to _____ 23, 13, p
Hannibal.fact: According to Polybius 23, 13, p.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Norman Schwarzkopf Jr., the commander of the Coalition of the Gulf War of _____–1991, claimed, "The technology of war may change, the sophistication of weapons certainly changes
Hannibal.fact: Norman Schwarzkopf Jr., the commander of the Coalition of the Gulf War of 1990–1991, claimed, "The technology of war may change, the sophistication of weapons certainly changes.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: No battle in history is a finer sample of tactics than _____
Hannibal.fact: No battle in history is a finer sample of tactics than Cannae.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Constantly overmatched by better soldiers, led by generals always respectable, often of great ability, he yet defied all their efforts to drive him from _____, for half a generation
Hannibal.fact: Constantly overmatched by better soldiers, led by generals always respectable, often of great ability, he yet defied all their efforts to drive him from Italy, for half a generation.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Excepting in the case of _____, and some few isolated instances, all wars up to the Second Punic War, had been decided largely, if not entirely, by battle-tactics
Hannibal.fact: Excepting in the case of Alexander, and some few isolated instances, all wars up to the Second Punic War, had been decided largely, if not entirely, by battle-tactics.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Hannibal's likeness is depicted on the Tunisian five-dinar bill issued on 8 November _____, as well as on a bill put into circulation on 20 March 2013
Hannibal.fact: Hannibal's likeness is depicted on the Tunisian five-dinar bill issued on 8 November 1993, as well as on a bill put into circulation on 20 March 2013.

Hannibal.subject: Ancient India
Hannibal.question: Plans envisage a mausoleum and a 17-metre (_____) high colossus of Hannibal on the Byrsa, the highest point of Carthage overlooking Tunis
Hannibal.fact: Plans envisage a mausoleum and a 17-metre (56 ft) high colossus of Hannibal on the Byrsa, the highest point of Carthage overlooking Tunis.

At the height of Harsha's power, his realm covered much of northern and northwestern India, with the Narmada River as its southern boundary.  He eventually made Kanyakubja (present-day Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh state) his imperial capital, and reigned until 647 CE.
